latin: E tenebris tantis tam clarum extollere lumen
en: Out of such great darkness you who first were able to raise

latin: qui primus potuisti inlustrans commoda vitae,
en: so clear a light, shining it on the good things of life,

latin: te sequor, o Graiae gentis decus, inque tuis nunc
en: you I follow, glory of the Greek race, and now in your

latin: ficta pedum pono pressis vestigia signis,
en: deep-pressed tracks I set down the planted prints of my feet,

latin: non ita certandi cupidus quam propter amorem
en: not so much from desire to compete as out of love,

latin: quod te imitari aveo; quid enim contendat hirundo
en: because I long to imitate you; for how should a swallow contend

latin: cycnis, aut quid nam tremulis facere artubus haedi
en: with swans, or what could kids on trembling legs

latin: consimile in cursu possint et fortis equi vis?
en: achieve in running to match the strong horse's force?

latin: tu, pater, es rerum inventor, tu patria nobis
en: You, father, are the discoverer of things; you supply us

latin: suppeditas praecepta, tuisque ex, inclute, chartis,
en: with a father's precepts, and from your pages, famous one,

latin: floriferis ut apes in saltibus omnia libant,
en: as bees in flowering glades sip at everything,

latin: omnia nos itidem depascimur aurea dicta,
en: so we likewise feed on all your golden sayings,

latin: aurea, perpetua semper dignissima vita.
en: golden, and always most worthy of perpetual life.

latin: nam simul ac ratio tua coepit vociferari
en: For as soon as your reasoning, sprung from a divine mind,

latin: naturam rerum divina mente coorta
en: begins to proclaim aloud the nature of things,

latin: diffugiunt animi terrores, moenia mundi
en: the terrors of the mind scatter and flee, the walls of the world

latin: discedunt. totum video per inane geri res.
en: draw apart; I see things carried on through the whole void.

latin: apparet divum numen sedesque quietae,
en: The power of the gods appears, and their quiet seats,

latin: quas neque concutiunt venti nec nubila nimbis
en: which neither winds shake nor clouds with rainstorms

latin: aspergunt neque nix acri concreta pruina
en: sprinkle, nor does snow, congealed by bitter frost,

latin: cana cadens violat semperque innubilus aether
en: falling white, do them violence; an ever-cloudless upper air

latin: integit et large diffuso lumine ridet:
en: covers them and laughs with light poured wide:

latin: omnia suppeditat porro natura neque ulla
en: nature, moreover, supplies them all things, and nothing

latin: res animi pacem delibat tempore in ullo.
en: at any time diminishes their peace of mind.

latin: at contra nusquam apparent Acherusia templa,
en: But on the other hand nowhere do the precincts of Acheron appear,

latin: nec tellus obstat quin omnia dispiciantur,
en: nor does the earth prevent all things from being seen

latin: sub pedibus quae cumque infra per inane geruntur.
en: that are carried on beneath our feet, below, through the void.

latin: his ibi me rebus quaedam divina voluptas
en: At these things a certain divine pleasure

latin: percipit atque horror, quod sic natura tua vi
en: and a shudder seize me there, that by your power nature

latin: tam manifesta patens ex omni parte retecta est.
en: lies so plainly open, laid bare on every side.

latin: Et quoniam docui, cunctarum exordia rerum
en: And since I have taught what the origins of all things

latin: qualia sint et quam variis distantia formis
en: are like, and how, differing in their various shapes,

latin: sponte sua volitent aeterno percita motu,
en: they fly of their own accord, driven by eternal motion,

latin: quove modo possint res ex his quaeque creari,
en: and in what way each thing can be created from them,

latin: hasce secundum res animi natura videtur
en: next after these things, it seems, the nature of the mind

latin: atque animae claranda meis iam versibus esse
en: and of the spirit must now be made clear in my verses,

latin: et metus ille foras praeceps Acheruntis agendus,
en: and that fear of Acheron driven headlong out of doors

latin: funditus humanam qui vitam turbat ab imo
en: which troubles human life from its very depths,

latin: omnia suffundens mortis nigrore neque ullam
en: suffusing all things with the blackness of death, and leaves

latin: esse voluptatem liquidam puramque relinquit.
en: no pleasure clear and pure.

latin: nam quod saepe homines morbos magis esse timendos
en: For though men often say that diseases are more to be feared,

latin: infamemque ferunt vitam quam Tartara leti
en: and a life of disgrace, than the Tartarus of death,

latin: et se scire animi naturam sanguinis esse,
en: and that they know the nature of the mind is of blood,

latin: aut etiam venti, si fert ita forte voluntas,
en: or else of wind, if so their fancy happens to run,

latin: nec prosum quicquam nostrae rationis egere,
en: and that they have no need whatever of our reasoning,

latin: hinc licet advertas animum magis omnia laudis
en: from this you may observe that all these things are boasted for the sake

latin: iactari causa quam quod res ipsa probetur.
en: of praise rather than because the thing itself is approved.

latin: extorres idem patria longeque fugati
en: These same men, exiled from their country and banished far

latin: conspectu ex hominum, foedati crimine turpi,
en: from the sight of men, befouled with some ugly charge,

latin: omnibus aerumnis adfecti denique vivunt,
en: afflicted, in short, with every hardship, still live on,

latin: et quo cumque tamen miseri venere parentant
en: and yet wherever they come in their misery they make offerings to the dead,

latin: et nigras mactant pecudes et manibus divis
en: and slaughter black cattle, and to the divine shades

latin: inferias mittunt multoque in rebus acerbis
en: send down funeral gifts, and in bitter circumstances

latin: acrius advertunt animos ad religionem.
en: turn their minds far more keenly to religion.

latin: quo magis in dubiis hominem spectare periclis
en: So it is the more fitting to watch a man in doubtful dangers

latin: convenit adversisque in rebus noscere qui sit;
en: and to learn in adversity what he is;

latin: nam verae voces tum demum pectore ab imo
en: for then at last true words are drawn up from the depth

latin: eliciuntur et eripitur persona amanare.
en: of the heart, and the mask is torn away; what is real remains.

latin: denique avarities et honorum caeca cupido,
en: Again, avarice and the blind craving for honors,

latin: quae miseros homines cogunt transcendere fines
en: which force wretched men to overstep the bounds

latin: iuris et inter dum socios scelerum atque ministros
en: of right, and sometimes, as partners and agents of crime,

latin: noctes atque dies niti praestante labore
en: to strive night and day with surpassing labor

latin: ad summas emergere opes, haec vulnera vitae
en: to rise up to the height of wealth: these wounds of life

latin: non minimam partem mortis formidine aluntur.
en: are fed in no small part by the fear of death.

latin: turpis enim ferme contemptus et acris egestas
en: For foul contempt and bitter want, as a rule,

latin: semota ab dulci vita stabilique videtur
en: seem far removed from a sweet and stable life,

latin: et quasi iam leti portas cunctarier ante;
en: and to linger, as it were, already before the gates of death;

latin: unde homines dum se falso terrore coacti
en: and while men, driven by a false terror, wish

latin: effugisse volunt longe longeque remosse,
en: to have fled far from these and removed themselves far, far away,

latin: sanguine civili rem conflant divitiasque
en: they amass a fortune from the blood of citizens, and greedily

latin: conduplicant avidi, caedem caede accumulantes,
en: double their riches, piling slaughter on slaughter;

latin: crudeles gaudent in tristi funere fratris
en: cruelly they rejoice at a brother's sad funeral,

latin: et consanguineum mensas odere timentque.
en: and hate and fear the tables of their kin.

latin: consimili ratione ab eodem saepe timore
en: On a like principle, and from this same fear, they are often

latin: macerat invidia ante oculos illum esse potentem,
en: wasted by envy: that before their eyes that man is powerful,

latin: illum aspectari, claro qui incedit honore,
en: that man is gazed at, who walks clothed in bright honor,

latin: ipsi se in tenebris volvi caenoque queruntur.
en: while they themselves, they complain, roll in darkness and mire.

latin: intereunt partim statuarum et nominis ergo.
en: Some perish for the sake of statues and a name.

latin: et saepe usque adeo, mortis formidine, vitae
en: And often, through fear of death, so great a hatred

latin: percipit humanos odium lucisque videndae,
en: of life and of seeing the light seizes human beings

latin: ut sibi consciscant maerenti pectore letum
en: that with grieving hearts they decree their own death,

latin: obliti fontem curarum hunc esse timorem:
en: forgetting that this fear is the fountain of their cares:

latin: hunc vexare pudorem, hunc vincula amicitiai
en: that this harasses shame, this bursts the bonds of friendship

latin: rumpere et in summa pietate evertere suadet:
en: and, in sum, urges them to overturn piety;

latin: nam iam saepe homines patriam carosque parentis
en: for often before now men have betrayed country and dear parents,

latin: prodiderunt vitare Acherusia templa petentes.
en: seeking to shun the precincts of Acheron.

latin: nam vel uti pueri trepidant atque omnia caecis
en: For just as children tremble and fear everything

latin: in tenebris metuunt, sic nos in luce timemus
en: in blind darkness, so we in the light are afraid

latin: inter dum, nihilo quae sunt metuenda magis quam
en: at times of things that are no more to be feared than

latin: quae pueri in tenebris pavitant finguntque futura.
en: what children in the dark shudder at and imagine will come.

latin: hunc igitur terrorem animi tenebrasque necessest
en: This terror of the mind, then, and this darkness

latin: non radii solis neque lucida tela diei
en: must be scattered not by the sun's rays or the bright shafts of day

latin: discutiant, sed naturae species ratioque.
en: but by the face and reasoning of nature.

latin: Primum animum dico, mentem quem saepe vocamus,
en: First, I say that the mind, which we often call thought,

latin: in quo consilium vitae regimenque locatum est,
en: in which the counsel and governance of life are placed,

latin: esse hominis partem nihilo minus ac manus et pes
en: is a part of a human being no less than hand and foot

latin: atque oculei partes animantis totius extant.
en: and eyes stand forth as parts of the whole living creature.

latin: sensum animi certa non esse in parte locatum,
en: that the sense of the mind is not placed in a fixed part,

latin: verum habitum quendam vitalem corporis esse,
en: but is a certain vital condition of the body,

latin: harmoniam Grai quam dicunt, quod faciat nos
en: which the Greeks call harmony, because it makes us

latin: vivere cum sensu, nulla cum in parte siet mens;
en: live with sense, though the mind is in no part;

latin: ut bona saepe valetudo cum dicitur esse
en: as when good health is often said to belong

latin: corporis, et non est tamen haec pars ulla valentis,
en: to the body, and yet it is not any part of the healthy man,

latin: sic animi sensum non certa parte reponunt;
en: so they do not place the sense of the mind in a fixed part;

latin: magno opere in quo mi diversi errare videntur.
en: and in this they seem to me to wander far astray.

latin: Saepe itaque, in promptu corpus quod cernitur, aegret,
en: And so the body, which is seen in plain view, is often sick,

latin: cum tamen ex alia laetamur parte latenti;
en: when yet in another, hidden part we are glad;

latin: et retro fit ubi contra sit saepe vicissim,
en: and in turn the reverse often happens, the other way about,

latin: cum miser ex animo laetatur corpore toto;
en: when one wretched in mind is glad in the whole body;

latin: non alio pacto quam si, pes cum dolet aegri,
en: in no other way than if, when a sick man's foot is aching,

latin: in nullo caput interea sit forte dolore.
en: his head meanwhile should happen to be in no pain.

latin: Praeterea molli cum somno dedita membra
en: Further, when the limbs are given up to soft sleep

latin: effusumque iacet sine sensu corpus honustum,
en: and the body, a heavy weight, lies sprawled without sense,

latin: est aliud tamen in nobis quod tempore in illo
en: there is yet something else in us which at that time

latin: multimodis agitatur et omnis accipit in se
en: is stirred in many ways and receives into itself

latin: laetitiae motus et curas cordis inanis.
en: all the motions of joy and the empty cares of the heart.

latin: Nunc animam quoque ut in membris cognoscere possis
en: Now, so that you may know the spirit too is in the limbs,

latin: esse neque harmonia corpus sentire solere,
en: and that the body does not feel by any harmony,

latin: principio fit uti detracto corpore multo
en: first of all it happens that when much of the body is taken away

latin: saepe tamen nobis in membris vita moretur.
en: life still often lingers in our limbs.

latin: Atque eadem rursum, cum corpora pauca caloris
en: And again this same life, when a few bodies of heat

latin: diffugere forasque per os est editus aegaër,
en: have scattered abroad and air has been driven out through the mouth,

latin: deserit extemplo venas atque ossa relinquit;
en: at once deserts the veins and leaves the bones;

latin: noscere ut hinc possis non aequas omnia partis
en: so that you may know from this that not all bodies

latin: corpora habere neque ex aequo fulcire salutem,
en: have an equal share, nor equally prop up our safety,

latin: sed magis haec, venti quae sunt calidique vaporis
en: but rather that these, which are seeds of wind and of warm

latin: semina, curare in membris ut vita moretur.
en: heat, see to it that life lingers in the limbs.

latin: est igitur calor ac ventus vitalis in ipso
en: There is therefore heat and a vital wind in the body

latin: corpore, qui nobis moribundos deserit artus.
en: itself, which deserts our limbs as we die.

latin: quapropter quoniam est animi natura reperta
en: Therefore, since the nature of the mind has been found,

latin: atque animae quasi pars hominis, redde harmoniai
en: and of the spirit, to be a kind of part of man, give back the name

latin: nomen, ad organicos alto delatum Heliconi,
en: of harmony, brought down to the musicians from lofty Helicon,

latin: sive aliunde ipsi porro traxere et in illam
en: or else they themselves drew it from elsewhere and carried it

latin: transtulerunt, proprio quae tum res nomine egebat.
en: over to that thing which then had need of a name of its own.

latin: quidquid id est, habeant: tu cetera percipe dicta.
en: Whatever it is, let them keep it; you, take in the rest of my words.

latin: Nunc animum atque animam dico coniuncta teneri
en: Now I say that mind and spirit are held joined together

latin: inter se atque unam naturam conficere ex se,
en: with one another and make up from themselves a single nature,

latin: sed caput esse quasi et dominari in corpore toto
en: but that the head, so to speak, the lord over the whole body,

latin: consilium, quod nos animum mentemque vocamus.
en: is the counsel which we call the mind and thought.

latin: idque situm media regione in pectoris haeret.
en: And this is set and fixed in the middle region of the breast.

latin: hic exultat enim pavor ac metus, haec loca circum
en: For here dread and fear leap up, around these places

latin: laetitiae mulcent: hic ergo mens animusquest.
en: joys caress us: here, therefore, are thought and mind.

latin: cetera pars animae per totum dissita corpus
en: The rest of the spirit, scattered through the whole body,

latin: paret et ad numen mentis momenque movetur.
en: obeys, and moves at the nod and impulse of the mind.

latin: idque sibi solum per se sapit et sibi gaudet,
en: This alone, of itself, knows for itself and is glad for itself,

latin: cum neque res animam neque corpus commovet una.
en: when nothing moves either the spirit or the body along with it.

latin: et quasi, cum caput aut oculus temptante dolore
en: And just as, when the head or the eye is hurt in us

latin: laeditur in nobis, non omni concruciamur
en: by an attack of pain, we are not tormented in our whole

latin: corpore, sic animus nonnumquam laeditur ipse
en: body, so the mind is sometimes hurt itself

latin: laetitiaque viget, cum cetera pars animai
en: or thrives with joy, when the rest of the spirit

latin: per membra atque artus nulla novitate cietur;
en: through the limbs and frame is stirred by nothing new;

latin: verum ubi vementi magis est commota metu mens,
en: but when the mind is moved by a more violent fear,

latin: consentire animam totam per membra videmus
en: we see the whole spirit through the limbs feel with it,

latin: sudoresque ita palloremque existere toto
en: and so sweat and pallor break out over the whole

latin: corpore et infringi linguam vocemque aboriri,
en: body, and the tongue falters and the voice dies away,

latin: caligare oculos, sonere auris, succidere artus,
en: the eyes grow dark, the ears ring, the limbs give way,

latin: denique concidere ex animi terrore videmus
en: and finally, from the mind's terror, we see

latin: saepe homines; facile ut quivis hinc noscere possit
en: men often collapse; so that anyone may easily learn from this

latin: esse animam cum animo coniunctam, quae cum animi vi
en: that the spirit is joined with the mind, and that, struck by the mind's

latin: percussa est, exim corpus propellit et icit.
en: force, it at once drives the body forward and strikes it.

latin: Haec eadem ratio naturam animi atque animai
en: This same reasoning teaches that the nature of mind and spirit

latin: corpoream docet esse; ubi enim propellere membra,
en: is bodily; for when it is seen to drive the limbs forward,

latin: corripere ex somno corpus mutareque vultum
en: to snatch the body from sleep and change the face,

latin: atque hominem totum regere ac versare videtur,
en: and to steer and turn the whole man,

latin: quorum nil fieri sine tactu posse videmus
en: none of which we see can happen without touch,

latin: nec tactum porro sine corpore, nonne fatendumst
en: nor touch, in turn, without body, must we not admit

latin: corporea natura animum constare animamque?
en: that mind and spirit consist of a bodily nature?

latin: praeterea pariter fungi cum corpore et una
en: Further, you see the mind is acted on together with the body

latin: consentire animum nobis in corpore cernis.
en: and feels along with it, in our body.

latin: si minus offendit vitam vis horrida teli
en: If the grim force of a weapon, though it does not strike out life,

latin: ossibus ac nervis disclusis intus adacta,
en: is driven in, laying open bones and sinews within,

latin: at tamen insequitur languor terraeque petitus
en: yet there follows a faintness, and a pleasant sinking

latin: suavis et in terra mentis qui gignitur aestus
en: to the earth, and, on the earth, the turmoil born in the mind,

latin: inter dumque quasi exsurgendi incerta voluntas.
en: and now and then a wavering will, as it were, to rise.

latin: ergo corpoream naturam animi esse necessest,
en: Therefore the nature of the mind must be bodily,

latin: corporeis quoniam telis ictuque laborat.
en: since it suffers from bodily weapons and their blow.

latin: Is tibi nunc animus quali sit corpore et unde
en: Now of what sort of body this mind of yours is, and from what

latin: constiterit pergam rationem reddere dictis.
en: it is composed, I shall go on to give an account in words.

latin: principio esse aio persuptilem atque minutis
en: To begin with, I say that it is exceedingly fine, and is made

latin: perquam corporibus factum constare. id ita esse
en: of exceedingly tiny bodies. That this is so

latin: hinc licet advertas animum, ut pernoscere possis.
en: you may turn your mind to here, so as to know it thoroughly.

latin: Nil adeo fieri celeri ratione videtur,
en: Nothing is seen to come about in so swift a way

latin: quam si mens fieri proponit et inchoat ipsa;
en: as what the mind proposes to happen and itself begins;

latin: ocius ergo animus quam res se perciet ulla,
en: therefore the mind stirs itself more quickly than any of the things

latin: ante oculos quorum in promptu natura videtur.
en: whose nature is seen plain before our eyes.

latin: at quod mobile tanto operest, constare rutundis
en: But what is so very mobile must consist of exceedingly round

latin: perquam seminibus debet perquamque minutis,
en: and exceedingly tiny seeds,

latin: momine uti parvo possint inpulsa moveri.
en: so that, struck by a small impulse, they can be moved.

latin: namque movetur aqua et tantillo momine flutat,
en: For water moves and flows at the slightest impulse,

latin: quippe volubilibus parvisque creata figuris.
en: being made, of course, of small shapes that roll.

latin: at contra mellis constantior est natura
en: But the nature of honey, by contrast, is more steady,

latin: et pigri latices magis et cunctantior actus:
en: its liquid more sluggish and its motion more delayed;

latin: haeret enim inter se magis omnis materiai
en: for the whole store of its matter clings more together,

latin: copia, ni mirum quia non tam levibus extat
en: surely because it is not made of bodies so smooth

latin: corporibus neque tam suptilibus atque rutundis.
en: nor so fine and round.

latin: namque papaveris aura potest suspensa levisque
en: For a hovering, light breath of air can make

latin: cogere ut ab summo tibi diffluat altus acervus,
en: a high heap of poppy seed flow away for you from the top,

latin: at contra lapidum coniectum spicarumque
en: but against a pile of stones or of ears of grain

latin: noenu potest. igitur parvissima corpora pro quam
en: it has no power. Therefore, as bodies are the smallest

latin: et levissima sunt, ita mobilitate fruuntur;
en: and smoothest, so they enjoy mobility;

latin: at contra quae cumque magis cum pondere magno
en: but whatever are found to be of greater weight

latin: asperaque inveniuntur, eo stabilita magis sunt.
en: and rougher, the more firmly they are fixed.

latin: nunc igitur quoniamst animi natura reperta
en: Now therefore, since the nature of the mind has been found

latin: mobilis egregie, perquam constare necessest
en: exceptionally mobile, it must consist of exceedingly

latin: corporibus parvis et levibus atque rutundis.
en: small and smooth and round bodies.

latin: quae tibi cognita res in multis, o bone, rebus
en: This fact, once known to you, my good friend, will be found useful

latin: utilis invenietur et opportuna cluebit.
en: in many matters and will be called timely.

latin: Haec quoque res etiam naturam dedicat eius,
en: This too reveals its nature,

latin: quam tenui constet textura quamque loco se
en: how thin the texture it is made of, and in how small

latin: contineat parvo, si possit conglomerari,
en: a place it would be held, if it could be gathered into a ball:

latin: quod simul atque hominem leti secura quies est
en: that as soon as the untroubled quiet of death has taken hold

latin: indepta atque animi natura animaeque recessit,
en: of a man, and the nature of mind and spirit has withdrawn,

latin: nil ibi libatum de toto corpore cernas
en: you could see nothing taken away there from the whole body

latin: ad speciem, nihil ad pondus: mors omnia praestat,
en: in appearance, nothing in weight: death leaves all intact

latin: vitalem praeter sensum calidumque vaporem.
en: except the vital sense and the warm heat.

latin: ergo animam totam perparvis esse necessest
en: Therefore the whole spirit must be of exceedingly small

latin: seminibus nexam per venas viscera nervos,
en: seeds, linked through veins, flesh, sinews,

latin: qua tenus, omnis ubi e toto iam corpore cessit,
en: inasmuch as, when all of it has gone from the whole body,

latin: extima membrorum circumcaesura tamen se
en: the outer contour of the limbs still keeps itself

latin: incolumem praestat nec defit ponderis hilum.
en: unharmed, and not one jot of weight is lacking.

latin: quod genus est, Bacchi cum flos evanuit aut cum
en: It is just as when the flower of Bacchus has died away, or when

latin: spiritus unguenti suavis diffugit in auras
en: the sweet breath of a perfume has scattered into the air,

latin: aut aliquo cum iam sucus de corpore cessit;
en: or when savor has departed from some body;

latin: nil oculis tamen esse minor res ipsa videtur
en: still the thing itself seems to the eyes no smaller

latin: propterea neque detractum de pondere quicquam,
en: for that, nor is anything taken from its weight,

latin: ni mirum quia multa minutaque semina sucos
en: surely because many tiny seeds make up

latin: efficiunt et odorem in toto corpore rerum.
en: the savors and the scent in the whole body of these things.

latin: quare etiam atque etiam mentis naturam animaeque
en: Therefore, again and again, the nature of mind and spirit

latin: scire licet perquam pauxillis esse creatam
en: you may know is made of exceedingly minute

latin: seminibus, quoniam fugiens nil ponderis aufert.
en: seeds, since when it flees it takes away no weight.

latin: Nec tamen haec simplex nobis natura putanda est.
en: Yet we must not think this nature simple.

latin: tenvis enim quaedam moribundos deserit aura
en: For a certain thin breath leaves the dying,

latin: mixta vapore, vapor porro trahit aeraaëra secum;
en: mixed with heat, and heat, in turn, draws air with it;

latin: nec calor est quisquam, cui non sit mixtus et aeraër;
en: nor is there any heat that has no air mixed in it;

latin: rara quod eius enim constat natura, necessest
en: for since its nature is of loose texture, it must be

latin: aerisaëris inter eum primordia multa moveri.
en: that many first-beginnings of air move within it.

latin: iam triplex animi est igitur natura reperta;
en: So now the nature of the mind is found to be threefold;

latin: nec tamen haec sat sunt ad sensum cuncta creandum,
en: and yet these are not enough, all together, to create sensation,

latin: nil horum quoniam recipit mens posse creare
en: since the mind does not accept that any of these can create

latin: sensiferos motus, quae denique mente volutat.
en: the sense-bearing motions, or what it then turns over in the mind.

latin: quarta quoque his igitur quaedam natura necessest
en: Therefore a certain fourth nature must also be

latin: adtribuatur; east omnino nominis expers;
en: added to these; it is altogether without a name;

latin: qua neque mobilius quicquam neque tenvius extat
en: than which nothing exists more mobile or more thin,

latin: nec magis e parvis et levibus ex elementis;
en: nor made of smaller and smoother elements;

latin: sensiferos motus quae didit prima per artus.
en: it is first to distribute the sense-bearing motions through the limbs.

latin: prima cietur enim, parvis perfecta figuris,
en: For it is first stirred, made as it is of small shapes;

latin: inde calor motus et venti caeca potestas
en: then heat takes up the motions, and the unseen power of wind,

latin: accipit, inde aeraër, inde omnia mobilitantur:
en: then air; then all things are set in motion:

latin: concutitur sanguis, tum viscera persentiscunt
en: the blood is shaken, then the flesh is thrilled through,

latin: omnia, postremis datur ossibus atque medullis
en: all of it; last it is passed to the bones and the marrow,

latin: sive voluptas est sive est contrarius ardor.
en: whether it is pleasure or the opposite burning.

latin: nec temere huc dolor usque potest penetrare neque acre
en: Nor can pain lightly penetrate this far, nor sharp

latin: permanare malum, quin omnia perturbentur
en: harm seep through, without all things being thrown into confusion

latin: usque adeo ut vitae desit locus atque animai
en: so far that life lacks room and the spirit's

latin: diffugiant partes per caulas corporis omnis.
en: parts scatter through all the passages of the body.

latin: sed plerumque fit in summo quasi corpore finis
en: But mostly an end is made, as it were, at the surface of the body

latin: motibus: hanc ob rem vitam retinere valemus.
en: to these motions: and for this reason we are able to hold on to life.

latin: Nunc ea quo pacto inter sese mixta quibusque
en: Now in what way these are mingled with one another, and in what

latin: compta modis vigeant rationem reddere aventem
en: modes arranged they thrive, though I am eager to give an account,

latin: abstrahit invitum patrii sermonis egestas;
en: the poverty of our native speech drags me back against my will;

latin: sed tamen, ut potero summatim attingere, tangam.
en: but still, as far as I can touch on it in sum, I shall touch it.

latin: inter enim cursant primordia principiorum
en: For the first-beginnings of the beginnings run among one another

latin: motibus inter se, nihil ut secernier unum
en: in their motions, so that no single one can be set apart

latin: possit nec spatio fieri divisa potestas,
en: nor its power be made separate by space,

latin: sed quasi multae vis unius corporis extant.
en: but they stand out, as it were, the many forces of one body.

latin: quod genus in quovis animantum viscere volgo
en: Just as in the flesh of any living thing, commonly,

latin: est odor et quidam color et sapor, et tamen ex his
en: there is smell and a certain color and savor, yet from all these

latin: omnibus est unum perfectum corporis augmen,
en: there is made up one complete growth of body,

latin: sic calor atque aeraër et venti caeca potestas
en: so heat and air and the unseen power of wind,

latin: mixta creant unam naturam et mobilis illa
en: mingled, create one nature, together with that mobile

latin: vis, initum motus ab se quae dividit ollis,
en: force which hands out from itself to them the beginning of motion,

latin: sensifer unde oritur primum per viscera motus.
en: from which the sense-bearing motion first arises through the flesh.

latin: nam penitus prorsum latet haec natura subestque
en: For this nature lies hidden deep down and underneath,

latin: nec magis hac infra quicquam est in corpore nostro
en: and there is nothing further below it in our body,

latin: atque anima est animae proporro totius ipsa.
en: and it is in its turn the very spirit of the whole spirit.

latin: quod genus in nostris membris et corpore toto
en: Just as in our limbs and through the whole body

latin: mixta latens animi vis est animaeque potestas,
en: the force of mind and the power of spirit lie mingled and hidden,

latin: corporibus quia de parvis paucisque creatast,
en: because it is created of bodies small and few,

latin: sic tibi nominis haec expers vis, facta minutis
en: so, you see, this force that has no name, made of minute

latin: corporibus, latet atque animae quasi totius ipsa
en: bodies, lies hidden, and is, as it were, the very spirit

latin: proporrost anima et dominatur corpore toto.
en: in its turn of the whole spirit, and rules through the whole body.

latin: consimili ratione necessest ventus et aeraër
en: On a like principle, wind and air and heat

latin: et calor inter se vigeant commixta per artus
en: must be active, mingled with one another through the limbs,

latin: atque aliis aliud subsit magis emineatque,
en: and one lie more beneath or stand out more than another,

latin: ut quiddam fieri videatur ab omnibus unum,
en: so that one thing may be seen to be made from them all,

latin: ni calor ac ventus seorsum seorsumque potestas
en: lest heat and wind apart, and apart the power

latin: aerisaëris interemant sensum diductaque solvant.
en: of air, should destroy sense and, drawn asunder, dissolve it.

latin: est etiam calor ille animo, quem sumit, in ira
en: The mind has also that heat which it takes on in anger,

latin: cum fervescit et ex oculis micat acrius ardor;
en: when it boils up and fire flashes more fiercely from the eyes;

latin: est et frigida multa, comes formidinis, aura,
en: there is also much cold breath, the companion of fear,

latin: quae ciet horrorem membris et concitat artus;
en: which stirs shuddering in the limbs and rouses the frame;

latin: est etiam quoque pacati status aerisaëris ille,
en: there is also that state of air made calm,

latin: pectore tranquillo fit qui voltuque sereno.
en: which comes about in a tranquil breast and a serene face.

latin: sed calidi plus est illis quibus acria corda
en: But there is more of the hot in those whose hearts are fierce

latin: iracundaque mens facile effervescit in ira,
en: and whose angry mind easily boils over into anger,

latin: quo genere in primis vis est violenta leonum,
en: of which kind above all is the violent force of lions,

latin: pectora qui fremitu rumpunt plerumque gementes
en: who often, groaning, burst their breasts with roaring

latin: nec capere irarum fluctus in pectore possunt.
en: and cannot contain the billows of their anger in their breast.

latin: at ventosa magis cervorum frigida mens est
en: But the cold mind of deer has more of wind

latin: et gelidas citius per viscera concitat auras,
en: and more quickly rouses icy breaths through the flesh,

latin: quae tremulum faciunt membris existere motum.
en: which make a trembling motion rise up in the limbs.

latin: at natura boum placido magis aereaëre vivit
en: But the nature of oxen lives more by calm air,

latin: nec nimis irai fax umquam subdita percit
en: nor ever does anger's smoky torch, set beneath, rouse it too far,

latin: fumida, suffundens caecae caliginis umbra,
en: spreading over it the shadow of blind darkness,

latin: nec gelidis torpet telis perfixa pavoris;
en: nor is it numbed, pierced through by the icy shafts of fear;

latin: interutrasque sitast cervos saevosque leones.
en: it is set between the two, the deer and the savage lions.

latin: sic hominum genus est: quamvis doctrina politos
en: So it is with the race of men: although training may make

latin: constituat pariter quosdam, tamen illa relinquit
en: some equally polished, still it leaves behind

latin: naturae cuiusque animi vestigia prima.
en: those first traces of the nature of each one's mind.

latin: nec radicitus evelli mala posse putandumst,
en: Nor must we think that faults can be torn out by the roots,

latin: quin proclivius hic iras decurrat ad acris,
en: so that one man does not run more readily to fierce anger,

latin: ille metu citius paulo temptetur, at ille
en: another not be assailed a little sooner by fear, a third

latin: tertius accipiat quaedam clementius aequo.
en: not take certain things more mildly than is right.

latin: inque aliis rebus multis differre necessest
en: And in many other things the varied natures of men

latin: naturas hominum varias moresque sequacis;
en: must differ, and the characters that follow on them;

latin: quorum ego nunc nequeo caecas exponere causas
en: whose hidden causes I cannot now set out,

latin: nec reperire figurarum tot nomina quot sunt
en: nor find as many names as there are shapes

latin: principiis, unde haec oritur variantia rerum.
en: of the beginnings, from which this variety of things arises.

latin: illud in his rebus video firmare potesse,
en: This I see that I can affirm in these matters:

latin: usque adeo naturarum vestigia linqui
en: that so slight are the traces of our natures left behind,

latin: parvola, quae nequeat ratio depellere nobis,
en: which reasoning cannot drive away from us,

latin: ut nihil inpediat dignam dis degere vitam.
en: that nothing hinders us from living a life worthy of gods.

latin: Haec igitur natura tenetur corpore ab omni
en: This nature, then, is held in by the whole body

latin: ipsaque corporis est custos et causa salutis;
en: and is itself the body's guardian and the cause of its safety;

latin: nam communibus inter se radicibus haerent
en: for they cling to one another by common roots

latin: nec sine pernicie divelli posse videntur.
en: and it seems they cannot be torn apart without destruction.

latin: quod genus e thuris glaebis evellere odorem
en: Just as to tear the smell from lumps of frankincense

latin: haud facile est, quin intereat natura quoque eius,
en: is not easy, without its nature too perishing,

latin: sic animi atque animae naturam corpore toto
en: so to draw out the nature of mind and spirit

latin: extrahere haut facile est, quin omnia dissoluantur.
en: from the whole body is not easy, without all being dissolved.

latin: inplexis ita principiis ab origine prima
en: So, with their beginnings interwoven from their first origin,

latin: inter se fiunt consorti praedita vita,
en: they come to be endowed with a life held in partnership,

latin: nec sibi quaeque sine alterius vi posse videtur
en: nor, it seems, can either, without the force of the other,

latin: corporis atque animi seorsum sentire potestas,
en: the power of body or of mind, feel apart, by itself,

latin: sed communibus inter eas conflatur utrimque
en: but by common motions between them on both sides

latin: motibus accensus nobis per viscera sensus.
en: sense is fanned and kindled for us through the flesh.

latin: Praeterea corpus per se nec gignitur umquam
en: Further, the body by itself is never born,

latin: nec crescit neque post mortem durare videtur.
en: nor grows, nor is seen to last after death.

latin: non enim, ut umor aquae dimittit saepe vaporem,
en: For not as the liquid of water often gives off the heat

latin: qui datus est, neque ea causa convellitur ipse,
en: that was given it, and is not for that reason torn apart itself,

latin: sed manet incolumis, non, inquam, sic animai
en: but stays unharmed, not so, I say, can the limbs, left behind,

latin: discidium possunt artus perferre relicti,
en: endure the separation of the spirit,

latin: sed penitus pereunt convulsi conque putrescunt.
en: but they perish utterly, torn apart, and rot away.

latin: ex ineunte aevo sic corporis atque animai
en: So from the beginning of life the mutual contacts

latin: mutua vitalis discunt contagia motus,
en: of body and spirit learn the motions of life,

latin: maternis etiam membris alvoque reposta,
en: even while laid away in the mother's limbs and womb,

latin: discidium ut nequeat fieri sine peste maloque;
en: so that separation cannot happen without ruin and harm;

latin: ut videas, quoniam coniunctast causa salutis,
en: so that you may see, since the cause of their safety is joined,

latin: coniunctam quoque naturam consistere eorum.
en: that their nature too must stand joined together.

latin: Quod super est, siquis corpus sentire refutat
en: For the rest, if anyone denies that the body feels

latin: atque animam credit permixtam corpore toto
en: and believes that the spirit, mingled through the whole body,

latin: suscipere hunc motum quem sensum nominitamus,
en: takes on this motion which we name sense,

latin: vel manifestas res contra verasque repugnat.
en: he fights against even plain and true facts.

latin: quid sit enim corpus sentire quis adferet umquam,
en: For who will ever tell us what it is for the body to feel,

latin: si non ipsa palam quod res dedit ac docuit nos?
en: if not what the thing itself has openly shown and taught us?

latin: 'at dimissa anima corpus caret undique sensu.'
en: "But when the spirit is let go, the body lacks sense in every part."

latin: perdit enim quod non proprium fuit eius in aevo
en: Yes, for it loses what was not its own in life,

latin: multaque praeterea perdit quom expellitur aevo.
en: and loses much besides when it is driven out of life.

latin: Dicere porro oculos nullam rem cernere posse,
en: Further, to say that the eyes can see nothing,

latin: sed per eos animum ut foribus spectare reclusis,
en: but that the mind looks out through them as through open doors,

latin: difficilest, contra cum sensus ducat eorum;
en: is hard, since the sense of the eyes leads us the other way;

latin: sensus enim trahit atque acies detrudit ad ipsas,
en: for sense drags us and thrusts us to the pupils themselves,

latin: fulgida praesertim cum cernere saepe nequimus,
en: especially since often we cannot see bright things,

latin: lumina luminibus quia nobis praepediuntur.
en: because the light of our eyes is hampered by light.

latin: quod foribus non fit; neque enim, qua cernimus ipsi,
en: This does not happen with doors; for the doorways through which

latin: ostia suscipiunt ullum reclusa laborem.
en: we ourselves look, when thrown open, take on no labor.

latin: praeterea si pro foribus sunt lumina nostra,
en: Further, if our eyes serve in place of doors,

latin: iam magis exemptis oculis debere videtur
en: then, it seems, the mind ought to see things better

latin: cernere res animus sublatis postibus ipsis.
en: with the eyes taken out, the very doorposts removed.

latin: Illud in his rebus nequaquam sumere possis,
en: In these matters you could by no means accept

latin: Democriti quod sancta viri sententia ponit,
en: what the holy judgment of the man Democritus lays down,

latin: corporis atque animi primordia singula primis
en: that the first-beginnings of body and of mind, one by one,

latin: adposita alternis, variare ac nectere membra.
en: set side by side alternately, diversify and knit the limbs.

latin: nam cum multo sunt animae elementa minora
en: For not only are the elements of the spirit much smaller

latin: quam quibus e corpus nobis et viscera constant,
en: than those of which our body and flesh are made,

latin: tum numero quoque concedunt et rara per artus
en: but also yield to them in number, and are sparsely scattered

latin: dissita sunt, dum taxat ut hoc promittere possis,
en: through the limbs, so that you may promise this much at least:

latin: quantula prima queant nobis iniecta ciere
en: as small as are the first bodies which, falling on us,

latin: corpora sensiferos motus in corpore, tanta
en: can stir sense-bearing motions in the body, so wide

latin: intervalla tenere exordia prima animai.
en: are the intervals the first origins of the spirit keep.

latin: nam neque pulveris inter dum sentimus adhaesum
en: For we do not feel at times the clinging of dust

latin: corpore nec membris incussam sidere cretam,
en: upon the body, nor chalk dashed on our limbs and settling there,

latin: nec nebulam noctu neque arani tenvia fila
en: nor do we feel mist at night, nor the spider's slender threads

latin: obvia sentimus, quando obretimur euntes,
en: meeting us, when we are netted in them as we go,

latin: nec supera caput eiusdem cecidisse vietam
en: nor the same spider's shriveled garment fallen on our head,

latin: vestem nec plumas avium papposque volantis,
en: nor the feathers of birds, nor the flying down of plants,

latin: qui nimia levitate cadunt plerumque gravatim,
en: which, from their great lightness, mostly fall only reluctantly,

latin: nec repentis itum cuiusvis cumque animantis
en: nor do we feel the passage of every creeping creature,

latin: sentimus nec priva pedum vestigia quaeque,
en: nor each single footprint, one by one,

latin: corpore quae in nostro culices et cetera ponunt.
en: that gnats and the rest set down upon our body.

latin: usque adeo prius est in nobis multa ciendum
en: So far must many things be stirred in us first

latin: quam primordia sentiscant concussa animai,
en: before the first-beginnings of the spirit, shaken, can feel,

latin: semina corporibus nostris inmixta per artus,
en: the seeds mixed with our bodies through the limbs,

latin: et quam in his intervallis tuditantia possint
en: and before, beating across these gaps, they can

latin: concursare coire et dissultare vicissim.
en: run together, unite, and leap apart in turn.

latin: Et magis est animus vitai claustra coercenscoërcens
en: And the mind holds the barriers of life more firmly

latin: et dominantior ad vitam quam vis animai.
en: and is more master over life than the force of spirit.

latin: nam sine mente animoque nequit residere per artus
en: For without thought and mind no part of the spirit

latin: temporis exiguam partem pars ulla animai,
en: can remain in the limbs for the smallest part of time,

latin: sed comes insequitur facile et discedit in auras
en: but follows readily as companion and departs into the air

latin: et gelidos artus in leti frigore linquit.
en: and leaves the limbs gone cold in the chill of death.

latin: at manet in vita cui mens animusque remansit,
en: But he stays in life in whom thought and mind remain,

latin: quamvis est circum caesis lacer undique membris;
en: however torn his trunk, with the limbs all round cut off;

latin: truncus adempta anima circum membrisque remota
en: the trunk, with spirit taken from around it and limbs removed,

latin: vivit et aetherias vitalis suscipit auras;
en: lives and draws in the life-giving airs of heaven;

latin: si non omnimodis, at magna parte animai
en: deprived, if not entirely, yet of a great part of its spirit,

latin: privatus, tamen in vita cunctatur et haeret;
en: it still lingers and holds fast in life;

latin: ut, lacerato oculo circum si pupula mansit
en: as, when the eye is torn all round, if the pupil remains

latin: incolumis, stat cernundi vivata potestas,
en: unharmed, the living power of seeing stands,

latin: dum modo ne totum corrumpas luminis orbem
en: provided only you do not ruin the whole orb of the eye

latin: et circum caedas aciem solamque relinquas;
en: and cut around the pupil and leave it all alone;

latin: id quoque enim sine pernicie non fiet eorum.
en: for that too will not happen without the destruction of both.

latin: at si tantula pars oculi media illa peresa est,
en: But if that tiny part in the middle of the eye is eaten away,

latin: occidit extemplo lumen tenebraeque secuntur,
en: at once the light sets and darkness follows,

latin: incolumis quamvis alioqui splendidus orbis.
en: though the bright orb be otherwise unharmed.

latin: hoc anima atque animus vincti sunt foedere semper.
en: By this covenant spirit and mind are always bound.

latin: Nunc age, nativos animantibus et mortalis
en: Come now, so you may know that in living creatures the minds

latin: esse animos animasque levis ut noscere possis,
en: and the light spirits are things born and mortal,

latin: conquisita diu dulcique reperta labore
en: verses long sought out and found with sweet labor

latin: digna tua pergam disponere carmina vita.
en: I shall go on to set out, worthy of your life.

latin: tu fac utrumque uno subiungas nomine eorum
en: You, see that you yoke both of them under one name,

latin: atque animam verbi causa cum dicere pergam,
en: and when, for example, I go on to speak of spirit,

latin: mortalem esse docens, animum quoque dicere credas,
en: teaching that it is mortal, believe that I speak of mind as well,

latin: qua tenus est unum inter se coniunctaque res est.
en: inasmuch as it is one thing, and a thing joined together.

latin: Principio quoniam tenuem constare minutis
en: To begin with, since I have shown that it is fine, and made

latin: corporibus docui multoque minoribus esse
en: of minute bodies, and formed of beginnings much smaller

latin: principiis factam quam liquidus umor aquai
en: than the flowing moisture of water

latin: aut nebula aut fumus —; nam longe mobilitate
en: or mist or smoke; for in mobility it far

latin: praestat et a tenui causa magis icta movetur,
en: excels, and moves when struck by a slighter cause;

latin: quippe ubi imaginibus fumi nebulaeque movetur;
en: indeed it is moved even by images of smoke and mist,

latin: quod genus in somnis sopiti ubi cernimus alte
en: as when, lulled in sleep, we see altars

latin: exhalare vaporem altaria ferreque fumum;
en: breathe their steam on high and send up smoke;

latin: nam procul haec dubio nobis simulacra gerunturaegerunturæ
en: for beyond doubt it is images that are borne to us here.

latin: nunc igitur quoniam quassatis undique vasis
en: Now therefore, since, when vessels are shattered on every side,

latin: diffluere umorem et laticem discedere cernis,
en: you see the moisture flow out and the liquid run away,

latin: et nebula ac fumus quoniam discedit in auras,
en: and since mist and smoke depart into the air,

latin: crede animam quoque diffundi multoque perire
en: believe that the spirit too is scattered, and perishes far

latin: ocius et citius dissolvi in corpora prima,
en: more swiftly, and is sooner dissolved into its first bodies,

latin: cum semel ex hominis membris ablata recessit;
en: once it has been taken from a man's limbs and has withdrawn;

latin: quippe etenim corpus, quod vas quasi constitit eius,
en: for indeed, since the body, which is as it were its vessel,

latin: cum cohibere nequit conquassatum ex aliqua re
en: cannot contain it when shaken apart by some cause

latin: ac rarefactum detracto sanguine venis,
en: and made rare by the drawing of blood from the veins,

latin: aereaëre qui credas posse hanc cohiberier ullo,
en: how could you believe it could be contained by any air,

latin: corpore qui nostro rarus magis incohibens sit?
en: which is rarer than our body and less able to contain?

latin: Praeterea gigni pariter cum corpore et una
en: Further, we feel that the mind is born together with the body,

latin: crescere sentimus pariterque senescere mentem.
en: and grows along with it, and along with it grows old.

latin: nam vel ut infirmo pueri teneroque vagantur
en: For just as children totter with a body weak

latin: corpore, sic animi sequitur sententia tenvis.
en: and tender, so a slender judgment of the mind goes with it.

latin: inde ubi robustis adolevit viribus aetas,
en: Then when their age has grown up into sturdy strength,

latin: consilium quoque maius et auctior est animi vis.
en: their counsel too is greater and the mind's force more increased.

latin: post ubi iam validis quassatum est viribus aevi
en: Later, when the body is shaken by the strong forces

latin: corpus et obtusis ceciderunt viribus artus,
en: of age, and the limbs have sunk with their strength blunted,

latin: claudicat ingenium, delirat lingua labat mens,
en: the wit limps, the tongue raves, the mind totters,

latin: omnia deficiunt atque uno tempore desunt.
en: all things fail and are lacking at one time.

latin: ergo dissolui quoque convenit omnem animai
en: It follows, therefore, that the whole nature of the spirit

latin: naturam, ceu fumus, in altas aerisaëris auras;
en: is dissolved as well, like smoke, into the high breezes of the air;

latin: quando quidem gigni pariter pariterque videmus
en: since we see it born alongside, and alongside

latin: crescere et, ut docui, simul aevo fessa fatisci.
en: grow, and, as I have shown, worn out by age, give way together.

latin: Huc accedit uti videamus, corpus ut ipsum
en: Add to this that we see, just as the body itself

latin: suscipere inmanis morbos durumque dolorem,

latin: sic animum curas acris luctumque metumque;

latin: quare participem leti quoque convenit esse.

latin: quin etiam morbis in corporis avius errat
en: What is more, in diseases of the body there often strays

latin: inter dumque gravi lethargo fertur in altum
en: and at times by a heavy lethargy is carried down into deep

latin: aeternumque soporem oculis nutuque cadenti;

latin: unde neque exaudit voces nec noscere voltus

latin: illorum potis est, ad vitam qui revocantes
en: the faces of those who, calling it back to life,

latin: circum stant lacrimis rorantes ora genasque.
en: stand around, wet with tears on face and cheek.

latin: quare animum quoque dissolui fateare necessest,
en: Therefore you must admit the mind too is dissolved,

latin: quandoquidem penetrant in eum contagia morbi;
en: since the contagions of disease make their way into it;

latin: nam dolor ac morbus leti fabricator uterquest,
en: for pain and disease are each of them craftsmen of death,

latin: multorum exitio perdocti quod sumus ante.

latin: et quoniam mentem sanari corpus ut aegrum
en: And since the mind, like a sick body, is healed

latin: consequitur gravitas membrorum, praepediuntur

latin: crura vacillanti, tardescit lingua, madet mens,

latin: at quae cumque queunt conturbari inque pediri,
en: But whatever things can be confused and hindered

en: show that, if a somewhat harsher cause worked its way in,

latin: causa, fore ut pereant aevo privata futuro.

latin: Quin etiam subito vi morbi saepe coactus
en: What is more, often, suddenly compelled by the force of disease,

latin: ante oculos aliquis nostros, ut fulminis ictu,

latin: concidit et spumas agit, ingemit et tremit artus,

latin: desipit, extentat nervos, torquetur, anhelat

latin: inconstanter, et in iactando membra fatigat,

latin: ni mirum quia vis morbi distracta per artus
en: no doubt because the force of the disease, dispersed through the limbs,

latin: turbat agens animam, spumans ut in aequore salso

latin: ventorum validis fervescunt viribus undae.

latin: exprimitur porro gemitus, quia membra dolore
en: Next, a groan is forced out, since the limbs are afflicted

latin: qua quasi consuerunt et sunt munita viai.

en: Loss of wits comes about because the force of mind and spirit

latin: conturbatur et, ut docui, divisa seorsum
en: is thrown into confusion and, as I have shown, split apart,

latin: disiectatur eodem illo distracta veneno.

latin: inde ubi iam morbi reflexit causa, reditque
en: Then when the cause of the disease has turned back, and the sharp

latin: in latebras acer corrupti corporis umor,

latin: tum quasi vaccillans primum consurgit et omnis
en: then first, as if tottering, he gets up, and to all

latin: paulatim redit in sensus animamque receptat.

latin: haec igitur tantis ubi morbis corpore in ipso
en: Since these, then, even within the body itself, are tossed

latin: iactentur miserisque modis distracta laborent,
en: by such great diseases, and suffer, torn apart in wretched ways,

latin: cur eadem credis sine corpore in aereaëre aperto
en: why do you believe that the same, without a body, in the open air,

latin: cum validis ventis aetatem degere posse?
en: can pass their lifetime among the strong winds?

latin: Et quoniam mentem sanari corpus ut aegrum
en: And since the mind, like a sick body, is healed,

latin: cernimus et flecti medicina posse videmus,
en: as we discern, and we see that it can be turned by medicine,

latin: id quoque praesagit mortalem vivere mentem.
en: this too foretells that the mind lives a mortal life.

latin: addere enim partis aut ordine traiecere aecumst
en: For he must add parts, or shift them from their order,

latin: aut aliquid prosum de summa detrahere hilum,

latin: commutare animum qui cumque adoritur et infit
en: for whoever sets about and begins to change the mind

latin: aut aliam quamvis naturam flectere quaerit.
en: or seeks to bend any other nature whatever.

latin: at neque transferri sibi partis nec tribui vult
en: But neither will it let parts be shifted in it, nor added,

latin: inmortale quod est quicquam neque defluere hilum;
en: that which is immortal, nor will it let one jot flow away;

latin: nam quod cumque suis mutatum finibus exit,
en: for whatever is changed and passes out of its own bounds,

latin: continuo hoc mors est illius quod fuit ante.
en: this at once is the death of what it was before.

latin: ergo animus sive aegrescit, mortalia signa
en: Therefore the mind, whether it sickens, gives out

latin: mittit, uti docui, seu flectitur a medicina.
en: mortal signs, as I have shown, or whether medicine turns it.

latin: usque adeo falsae rationi vera videtur
en: So surely does the true thing seem to meet false reasoning

latin: res occurrere et effugium praecludere eunti
en: and bar its escape as it goes

latin: ancipitique refutatu convincere falsum.
en: and convict the false with a two-edged refutation.

latin: Denique saepe hominem paulatim cernimus ire
en: Finally, we often see a man go little by little

latin: et membratim vitalem deperdere sensum;
en: and lose the vital sense limb by limb:

latin: in pedibus primum digitos livescere et unguis,
en: first the toes on the feet and the nails turn livid,

latin: inde pedes et crura mori, post inde per artus
en: then the feet and legs die, then after that through the other

latin: ire alios tractim gelidi vestigia leti.
en: limbs the tracks of chill death go creeping.

latin: scinditur atque animae haec quoniam natura nec uno
en: Since this nature of the spirit is split and does not

latin: tempore sincera existit, mortalis habendast.
en: come forth whole at one time, it must be held mortal.

latin: quod si forte putas ipsam se posse per artus
en: But if perhaps you think it can draw itself inward

latin: introsum trahere et partis conducere in unum
en: through the limbs and gather its parts into one,

latin: atque ideo cunctis sensum diducere membris,
en: and so withdraw sense from all the limbs,

latin: at locus ille tamen, quo copia tanta animai
en: yet that place where so great a store of spirit

latin: cogitur, in sensu debet maiore videri;
en: is gathered ought to be seen to have greater sense;

latin: qui quoniam nusquamst, ni mirum, ut diximus ante,
en: and since it is nowhere, no doubt, as we said before,

latin: dilaniata foras dispargitur, interit ergo.
en: the spirit, torn apart, is scattered abroad and so perishes.

latin: quin etiam si iam libeat concedere falsum
en: What is more, even if we chose to grant what is false

latin: et dare posse animam glomerari in corpore eorum,
en: and allow that the spirit can be massed in the body of those

latin: lumina qui lincunt moribundi particulatim,
en: who leave the light, dying bit by bit,

latin: mortalem tamen esse animam fateare necesse
en: still you must admit the spirit is mortal,

latin: nec refert utrum pereat dispersa per auras
en: nor does it matter whether it perishes scattered through the air

latin: an contracta suis e partibus obbrutescat,
en: or, drawn in out of its parts, grows dull and brutish,

latin: quando hominem totum magis ac magis undique sensus
en: since more and more, on every side, sense fails

latin: deficit et vitae minus et minus undique restat.
en: the whole man, and less and less of life remains on every side.

latin: Et quoniam mens est hominis pars una locoque
en: And since the mind is a single part of a man and stays

latin: fixa manet certo, vel ut aures atque oculi sunt
en: fixed in a certain place, just as the ears and eyes are,

latin: atque alii sensus qui vitam cumque gubernant,
en: and the other senses that steer our life,

latin: et vel uti manus atque oculus naresve seorsum
en: and since, just as hand or eye or nostrils, set apart

latin: secreta ab nobis nequeunt sentire neque esse,
en: and severed from us, cannot feel or even be,

latin: sed tamen in parvo lincuntur tempore tali,
en: but yet, in such a state, are abandoned in a short time,

latin: sic animus per se non quit sine corpore et ipso
en: so the mind cannot by itself be without the body and the man

latin: esse homine, illius quasi quod vas esse videtur,
en: himself, which seems to be a kind of vessel for it,

latin: sive aliud quid vis potius coniunctius ei
en: or whatever else you would rather picture as more closely

latin: fingere, quandoquidem conexu corpus adhaeret.
en: joined to it, since the body clings to it with a bond.

latin: Denique corporis atque animi vivata potestas
en: Again, the living powers of body and mind

latin: inter se coniuncta valent vitaque fruuntur;
en: have strength and enjoy life only joined to each other;

latin: nec sine corpore enim vitalis edere motus
en: for neither without the body can it put forth the motions of life,

latin: sola potest animi per se natura nec autem
en: the nature of the mind, alone by itself, nor again

latin: cassum anima corpus durare et sensibus uti.
en: can a body deprived of spirit endure and use its senses.

latin: scilicet avolsus radicibus ut nequit ullam
en: Clearly, just as the eye itself, torn out by the roots,

latin: dispicere ipse oculus rem seorsum corpore toto,
en: cannot make out any thing apart from the whole body,

latin: sic anima atque animus per se nil posse videtur.
en: so the spirit and the mind by themselves seem to have no power.

latin: ni mirum quia per venas et viscera mixtim,
en: No wonder, since, mingled through veins and flesh,

latin: per nervos atque ossa tenentur corpore ab omni
en: through sinews and bones, they are held in by the whole body,

latin: nec magnis intervallis primordia possunt
en: and their first-beginnings cannot leap apart freely

latin: libera dissultare, ideo conclusa moventur
en: across great intervals; therefore, shut in, they move

latin: sensiferos motus, quos extra corpus in auras
en: with the sense-bearing motions which, outside the body,

latin: aerisaëris haut possunt post mortem eiecta moveri
en: cast out into the breezes of air after death, they cannot move,

latin: propterea quia non simili ratione tenentur;
en: because they are not held in by a like principle;

latin: corpus enim atque animans erit aeraër, si cohibere
en: for air would be a body, a living thing, if the spirit

latin: sese anima atque in eos poterit concludere motus,

latin: quos ante in nervis et in ipso corpore agebat.
en: which before it carried on in the sinews and in the body itself.

latin: quare etiam atque etiam resoluto corporis omni
en: Therefore again and again, when the whole covering of the body

latin: tegmine et eiectis extra vitalibus auris
en: is undone and the breaths of life are cast out,

latin: dissolui sensus animi fateare necessest
en: you must admit that the senses of the mind are dissolved,

latin: atque animam, quoniam coniunctast causa duobus.
en: and the spirit too, since the cause of the two is joined.

latin: Denique cum corpus nequeat perferre animai
en: Again, since the body cannot endure the parting

latin: discidium, quin in taetro tabescat odore,

latin: quid dubitas quin ex imo penitusque coorta
en: why do you doubt that, risen from deep within, from the depths,

latin: emanarit uti fumus diffusa animae vis,
en: the force of the spirit has flowed out, diffused like smoke,

latin: atque ideo tanta mutatum putre ruina
en: and that therefore the body, changed and rotten, has collapsed

latin: conciderit corpus, penitus quia mota loco sunt

latin: fundamenta foras manant animaeque per artus
en: deep from their place, and flow outward through the limbs

latin: perque viarum omnis flexus, in corpore qui sunt,

latin: atque foramina? multimodis ut noscere possis

latin: et prius esse sibi distractam corpore in ipso,

latin: quam prolapsa foras enaret in aerisaëris auras.
en: before it slipped out and swam forth into the breezes of air.

latin: Quin etiam finis dum vitae vertitur intra,
en: What is more, while it still turns within the bounds of life,

latin: saepe aliqua tamen e causa labefacta videtur

latin: ire anima ac toto solui de corpore tota

latin: et quasi supremo languescere tempore voltus
en: and the face seems to grow faint as at the final hour

latin: molliaque exsangui cadere omnia corpore membra.

latin: aut animam liquisse; ubi iam trepidatur et omnes

latin: conquassatur enim tum mens animaeque potestas

latin: non modo non omnem possit durare per aevom,

latin: sed minimum quodvis nequeat consistere tempus?

latin: nec sibi enim quisquam moriens sentire videtur

latin: ire foras animam incolumem de corpore toto,

latin: nec prius ad iugulum et supera succedere fauces,
en: nor rising first to the throat and the gullet above,

latin: verum deficere in certa regione locatam;
en: but failing, placed as it is in a fixed region,

latin: ut sensus alios in parti quemque sua scit
en: just as he knows the other senses dissolve, each in its own

latin: dissolui. quod si inmortalis nostra foret mens,
en: part. But if our mind were immortal,

latin: non tam se moriens dissolvi conquereretur,

en: Again, why is the thought and judgment of the mind never

latin: sedibus et certis regionibus omnibus haeret,

latin: si non certa loca ad nascendum reddita cuique

latin: sunt, et ubi quicquid possit durare creatum
en: and where each thing, once created, can endure,

latin: atque ita multimodis partitis artubus esse,

latin: membrorum ut numquam existat praeposterus ordo?

latin: si subito medium celeri praeciderit ictu

latin: dispertita procul dubio quoque vis animai

latin: mobilitate mali non quit sentire dolorem;

latin: et simul in pugnae studio quod dedita mens est,

en: a serpent's, with its long body, both of them

latin: omnia iam sorsum cernes ancisa recenti

latin: volnere tortari et terram conspargere tabo,
en: still fresh, writhe and sprinkle the earth with gore,

latin: ipsam seque retro partem petere ore priorem,
en: and the fore part turn back to seek itself with its mouth,

latin: volneris ardenti ut morsu premat icta dolore.
en: to grip with its bite, struck by the burning pain of the wound.

latin: omnibus esse igitur totas dicemus in illis
en: Shall we say, then, that there are whole spirits in all those

en: Therefore that which was one has been divided along with

latin: in multas quoniam partis disciditur aeque.

en: Further, if the nature of the spirit is immortal

latin: nec vestigia gestarum rerum ulla tenemus?

latin: non, ut opinor, id ab leto iam longius errat;

latin: interiisse, et quae nunc est nunc esse creatam.

latin: tum cum gignimur et vitae cum limen inimus,
