latin: haud ita conveniebat uti cum corpore et una
en: it would not then be fitting that, with the body and together

latin: cum membris videatur in ipso sanguine cresse,
en: with the limbs, it should be seen to grow within the very blood,

latin: sed vel ut in cavea per se sibi vivere solam
en: but fitting rather that it live alone, for itself, as in a cage,

latin: convenit, ut sensu corpus tamen affluat omne.
en: and yet in such a way that the whole body flows with sense.

latin: quare etiam atque etiam neque originis esse putandumst
en: Therefore, again and again, we must not think that spirits

latin: expertis animas nec leti lege solutas;
en: are without a beginning, nor released from the law of death;

latin: nam neque tanto opere adnecti potuisse putandumst
en: for we must not think they could have been bound so closely

latin: corporibus nostris extrinsecus insinuatas,
en: to our bodies, having worked their way in from outside,

latin: quod fieri totum contra manifesta docet res
en: a thing the plain fact shows to be wholly the reverse;

latin: aenamqueænamque ita conexa est per venas viscera nervos
en: for the spirit is so knit through veins, flesh, sinews,

latin: ossaque, uti dentes quoque sensu participentur;
en: and bones, that even the teeth are given a share in sense,

latin: morbus ut indicat et gelidai stringor aquai
en: as toothache shows, and the twinge of icy water,

latin: et lapis oppressus subitis e frugibus asperaeasperæ
en: and a rough stone bitten on, met suddenly in the bread;

latin: nec, tam contextae cum sint, exire videntur
en: nor, since they are so closely woven in, do they seem able

latin: incolumes posse et salvas exsolvere sese
en: to go out unharmed and unloose themselves safe

latin: omnibus e nervis atque ossibus articulisque,
en: from all the sinews and the bones and joints.

latin: quod si forte putas extrinsecus insinuatam
en: But if perhaps you think the spirit, working in from outside,

latin: permanare animam nobis per membra solere,
en: is wont to make its way, seeping, through our limbs,

latin: tanto quique magis cum corpore fusa peribit;
en: so much the more surely will it perish, being fused with the body;

latin: quod permanat enim, dissolvitur, interit ergo;
en: for what seeps through is dissolved, and therefore perishes;

latin: dispertitur enim per caulas corporis omnis.
en: for it is parted out through all the passages of the body.

latin: ut cibus, in membra atque artus cum diditur omnis,
en: As food, when it is dispersed into all the limbs and frame,

latin: disperit atque aliam naturam sufficit ex se,
en: perishes and supplies another nature out of itself,

latin: sic anima atque animus quamvis est integra recens in
en: so spirit and mind, however whole they go fresh

latin: corpus eunt, tamen in manando dissoluuntur,
en: into the body, are yet dissolved in seeping through,

latin: dum quasi per caulas omnis diduntur in artus
en: while, as through passages, there are dispersed into all the frame

latin: particulae quibus haec animi natura creatur,
en: the tiny parts of which this nature of the mind is created,

latin: quae nunc in nostro dominatur corpore nata
en: the nature which now has mastery in our body, born

latin: ex illa quae tunc periit partita per artus.
en: from that which perished then, parted through the frame.

latin: quapropter neque natali privata videtur
en: Therefore it seems the nature of the spirit is neither

latin: esse die natura animae nec funeris expers.
en: deprived of a birthday nor exempt from a funeral.

latin: Semina praeterea linquontur necne animai
en: Again, are seeds of the spirit left behind, or not,

latin: corpore in exanimo? quod si lincuntur et insunt,
en: in the lifeless body? If they are left and are in it,

latin: haut erit ut merito inmortalis possit haberi,
en: there will be no way it can rightly be held immortal,

latin: partibus amissis quoniam libata recessit.
en: since it has gone off diminished, with parts lost.

latin: sin ita sinceris membris ablata profugit,
en: But if it has fled away, taken off with its parts so intact

latin: ut nullas partis in corpore liquerit ex se,
en: that it has left no parts of itself in the body,

latin: unde cadavera rancenti iam viscere vermes
en: from where do corpses, their flesh now going rancid,

latin: expirant atque unde animantum copia tanta
en: breathe out worms, and from where so great a host of living things,

latin: exos et exanguis tumidos perfluctuat artus?
en: boneless and bloodless, surge through the swollen frame?

latin: quod si forte animas extrinsecus insinuari?
en: But if perhaps you believe that spirits work their way in from outside

latin: vermibus et privas in corpora posse venire
en: into worms, and can come one by one into bodies,

latin: credis nec reputas cur milia multa animarum
en: and do not reckon why many thousands of spirits

latin: conveniant unde una recesserit, hoc tamen est ut
en: should gather where one has withdrawn, still there is this

latin: quaerendum videatur et in discrimen agendum,
en: that it seems must be asked and brought to decision:

latin: utrum tandem animae venentur semina quaeque
en: whether, in the end, the spirits hunt down each of the seeds

latin: vermiculorum ipsaeque sibi fabricentur ubi sint,
en: of little worms and build themselves a place to be,

latin: an quasi corporibus perfectis insinuentur.
en: or work their way, as it were, into bodies already complete.

latin: at neque cur faciant ipsae quareve laborent
en: But why they should do it themselves, or why they should labor,

latin: dicere suppeditat. neque enim, sine corpore cum sunt,
en: there is no saying. For indeed, when they are without a body,

latin: sollicitae volitant morbis alguque fameque;
en: they do not flit about troubled by diseases and cold and hunger;

latin: corpus enim magis his vitiis adfine laborat,
en: for it is the body, more akin to these ills, that suffers them,

latin: et mala multa animus contage fungitur eius.
en: and the mind endures many evils by contact with it.

latin: sed tamen his esto quamvis facere utile corpus,
en: But grant it as useful as you like for them to make a body

latin: cum subeant; at qua possint via nulla videtur.
en: when they come in under; yet there seems no way they could.

latin: haut igitur faciunt animae sibi corpora et artus.
en: Therefore spirits do not make bodies and frames for themselves.

latin: nec tamen est ut qui cum perfectis insinuentur
en: Nor yet is there a way they could work their way into bodies

latin: corporibus; neque enim poterunt suptiliter esse
en: already complete; for neither could they be finely

latin: conexae neque consensu contagia fient.
en: knit in, nor will contact be made through shared feeling.

latin: Denique cur acris violentia triste leonum
en: Again, why does fierce violence go with the grim breed

latin: seminium sequitur, volpes dolus, et fuga cervos?
en: of lions, cunning with foxes, and flight with deer,

latin: a patribus datur et a patrius pavor incitat artus,
en: handed down from their sires, their sires' fear spurring their frame,

latin: et iam cetera de genere hoc cur omnia membris
en: and why indeed do all other things of this kind

latin: ex ineunte aevo generascunt ingenioque,
en: come to be in limbs and temper from the beginning of life,

latin: si non, certa suo quia semine seminioque
en: if not because, fixed by its own seed and breed,

latin: vis animi pariter crescit cum corpore quoque?
en: the force of the mind grows equally with every body?

latin: quod si inmortalis foret et mutare soleret
en: But if it were immortal and used to change

latin: corpora, permixtis animantes moribus essent,
en: bodies, living things would have mixed characters:

latin: effugeret canis Hyrcano de semine saepe
en: the dog of Hyrcanian seed would often flee

latin: cornigeri incursum cervi tremeretque per auras
en: the charge of the horned stag, and the hawk would tremble

latin: aerisaëris accipiter fugiens veniente columba,
en: through the breezes of the air, fleeing at the coming of the dove,

latin: desiperent homines, saperent fera saecla ferarum.
en: men would lack sense, and the wild generations of wild beasts be wise.

latin: illud enim falsa fertur ratione, quod aiunt
en: For that rests on false reasoning, when they say

latin: inmortalem animam mutato corpore flecti;
en: an immortal spirit is altered when its body is changed;

latin: quod mutatur enim, dissolvitur, interit ergo;
en: for what is changed is dissolved, and therefore perishes;

latin: traiciuntur enim partes atque ordine migrant;
en: for its parts are transposed and shift from their order;

latin: quare dissolui quoque debent posse per artus,
en: therefore they must be able to be dissolved through the frame too,

latin: denique ut intereant una cum corpore cunctae.
en: so that in the end they all perish together with the body.

latin: sin animas hominum dicent in corpora semper
en: But if they say that the spirits of men always pass

latin: ire humana, tamen quaeram cur e sapienti
en: into human bodies, still I shall ask why from wise

latin: stulta queat fieri, nec prudens sit puer ullus,
en: a spirit could turn foolish, and why no boy is prudent,

latin: si non, certa suo quia semine seminioque
en: if not because, fixed by its own seed and breed,

latin: nec tam doctus equae pullus quam fortis equi vis.
en: nor the mare's foal as well trained as the strong horse's force.

latin: scilicet in tenero tenerascere corpore mentem
en: No doubt they will take refuge in this: that in a tender body

latin: confugient. quod si iam fit, fateare necessest
en: the mind grows tender. But if this happens, you must confess

latin: mortalem esse animam, quoniam mutata per artus
en: that the spirit is mortal, since, changed throughout the frame,

latin: tanto opere amittit vitam sensumque priorem.
en: it loses so greatly its former life and sense.

latin: quove modo poterit pariter cum corpore quoque
en: Or how will it be able, in step with every body,

latin: confirmata cupitum aetatis tangere florem
en: to grow strong and touch the longed-for flower of age,

latin: vis animi, nisi erit consors in origine prima?
en: this force of the mind, unless it is a partner at the first origin?

latin: quidve foras sibi vult membris exire senectis?
en: Or why does it wish to go out of limbs grown old?

latin: an metuit conclusa manere in corpore putri
en: Does it fear to stay shut up in a rotting body,

latin: et domus aetatis spatio ne fessa vetusto
en: fear that its house, worn out by the long length of years,

latin: obruat? at non sunt immortali ulla pericla.
en: may fall in on it? But there are no dangers for the immortal.

latin: Denique conubia ad Veneris partusque ferarum
en: Again, that spirits stand ready at the couplings of Venus

latin: esse animas praesto deridiculum esse videtur,
en: and the births of beasts seems a thing to laugh at,

latin: expectare immortalis mortalia membra
en: immortals waiting for mortal limbs

latin: innumero numero certareque praeproperanter
en: in number beyond number, and contending headlong

latin: inter se quae prima potissimaque insinuetur;
en: among themselves which first and before all shall work its way in;

latin: si non forte ita sunt animarum foedera pacta,
en: unless perhaps the covenants of spirits are so agreed

latin: ut quae prima volans advenerit insinuetur
en: that whichever comes flying first works its way in

latin: prima neque inter se contendant viribus hilum.
en: first, and they do not strive with their strength one whit.

latin: Denique in aethere non arbor, non aequore in alto
en: Again, there can be no tree in the upper air, no clouds

latin: nubes esse queunt nec pisces vivere in arvis
en: in the deep sea, nor can fish live in the fields,

latin: nec cruor in lignis neque saxis sucus inesse.
en: nor blood be in wood, nor sap in stones.

latin: certum ac dispositumst ubi quicquid crescat et insit.
en: It is fixed and ordered where each thing grows and is.

latin: sic animi natura nequit sine corpore oriri
en: So the nature of the mind cannot arise without the body,

latin: sola neque a nervis et sanguine longius esse.
en: alone, nor exist far off from sinews and blood.

latin: quod si posset enim, multo prius ipsa animi vis
en: For if it could, the force of the mind itself, much sooner,

latin: in capite aut umeris aut imis calcibus esse
en: could be in the head or shoulders or the lowest heels,

latin: posset et innasci quavis in parte soleret,
en: and would be wont to be born in any part you please,

latin: tandem in eodem homine atque in eodem vase manere.
en: and still remain in the same man and the same vessel.

latin: quod quoniam nostro quoque constat corpore certum
en: And since even in our body it is evidently fixed

latin: dispositumque videtur ubi esse et crescere possit
en: and ordered, it seems, where each can be and grow,

latin: sorsum anima atque animus, tanto magis infitiandum
en: spirit and mind, each apart, all the more must we deny

latin: totum posse extra corpus durare genique.
en: that it can, entire, endure outside the body, or be born.

latin: quare, corpus ubi interiit, periisse necessest
en: Therefore, when the body has perished, you must confess

latin: confiteare animam distractam in corpore toto.
en: that the spirit has perished, torn apart through the whole body.

latin: quippe etenim mortale aeterno iungere et una
en: For indeed, to join the mortal to the eternal, and to think

latin: consentire putare et fungi mutua posse
en: that they can feel together and act each upon each,

latin: desiperest; quid enim diversius esse putandumst
en: is folly; for what must be thought more at odds

latin: aut magis inter se disiunctum discrepitansque,
en: or more disjoined from each other and more discordant

latin: quam mortale quod est inmortali atque perenni
en: than that what is mortal, joined to the immortal

latin: iunctum in concilio saevas tolerare procellas?
en: and everlasting in union, should bear savage storms?

latin: praeterea quaecumque manent aeterna necessest
en: Further, whatever things endure eternal must, of necessity,

latin: aut quia sunt solido cum corpore respuere ictus
en: either, because they are of solid body, repel blows

latin: nec penetrare pati sibi quicquam quod queat artas
en: and suffer nothing to enter them that could tear apart

latin: dissociare intus partis, ut materiai
en: their close-knit parts within, as the bodies of matter

latin: corpora sunt, quorum naturam ostendimus ante,
en: are, whose nature we have shown before;

latin: aut ideo durare aetatem posse per omnem,
en: or be able to last through all time for this reason,

latin: plagarum quia sunt expertia sicut inanest,
en: that they are exempt from blows, as the void is,

latin: quod manet intactum neque ab ictu fungitur hilum,
en: which stays untouched and is not affected one whit by a stroke;

latin: aut etiam quia nulla loci sit copia circum,
en: or else because there is no supply of place around them

latin: quo quasi res possint discedere dissoluique,
en: into which things could, as it were, part and be dissolved,

latin: sicut summarum summast aeterna, neque extra
en: as the sum of sums is eternal, nor is there outside it

latin: quis locus est quo diffugiant neque corpora sunt quae
en: any place into which they might scatter, nor are there bodies that

latin: possint incidere et valida dissolvere plaga.
en: could fall upon them and dissolve them with a strong blow.

latin: Quod si forte ideo magis inmortalis habendast,
en: But if perhaps it should rather be held immortal for this reason,

latin: quod vitalibus ab rebus munita tenetur,
en: that it is kept fortified by the things that give it life,

latin: aut quia non veniunt omnino aliena salutis,
en: either because things foreign to its safety do not come at all,

latin: aut quia quae veniunt aliqua ratione recedunt
en: or because those that do come are by some means driven back

latin: pulsa prius quam quid noceant sentire queamus,
en: and retreat before we can feel what harm they do,

latin: praeter enim quam quod morbis cum corporis aegret,
en: for besides that it sickens along with the body's diseases,

latin: advenit id quod eam de rebus saepe futuris
en: there comes that which often torments it about things to come,

latin: macerat inque metu male habet curisque fatigat,
en: keeps it wretched in fear, and wears it out with cares,

latin: praeteritisque male admissis peccata remordent.
en: and for misdeeds in the past its sins gnaw it with remorse.

latin: adde furorem animi proprium atque oblivia rerum,
en: Add the madness proper to the mind, and its forgetfulness of things;

latin: adde quod in nigras lethargi mergitur undas.
en: add that it is plunged into the black waves of lethargy.

latin: Nil igitur mors est ad nos neque pertinet hilum,
en: Death, therefore, is nothing to us, and concerns us not a whit,

latin: quandoquidem natura animi mortalis habetur.
en: since the nature of the mind is held to be mortal.

latin: et vel ut ante acto nihil tempore sensimus aegri,
en: And just as in time gone by we felt no distress

latin: ad confligendum venientibus undique Poenis,
en: when the Carthaginians were coming from every side to the clash,

latin: omnia cum belli trepido concussa tumultu
en: when all things, shaken by the trembling tumult of war,

latin: horrida contremuere sub altis aetheris auris,
en: shuddered and quaked beneath the high breezes of the upper air,

latin: in dubioque fuere utrorum ad regna cadendum
en: and it stood in doubt under which side's rule all men

latin: omnibus humanis esset terraque marique,
en: must fall, all that is human, by land and by sea,

latin: sic, ubi non erimus, cum corporis atque animai
en: so, when we shall not be, when the parting of body and spirit

latin: discidium fuerit, quibus e sumus uniter apti,
en: has come about, from which we are joined and fitted into one,

latin: scilicet haud nobis quicquam, qui non erimus tum,
en: surely nothing at all, to us who then shall not be,

latin: accidere omnino poterit sensumque movere,
en: will be able to happen or to move our sense,

latin: non si terra mari miscebitur et mare caelo.
en: not if earth should be mingled with sea, and sea with sky.

latin: et si iam nostro sentit de corpore postquam
en: And even if it does feel, after it is torn from our body,

latin: distractast animi natura animaeque potestas,
en: the nature of the mind along with the power of the spirit,

latin: nil tamen est ad nos, qui comptu coniugioque
en: still it is nothing to us, who by the joining and wedlock

latin: corporis atque animae consistimus uniter apti.
en: of body and spirit exist, joined and fitted into one.

latin: nec, si materiem nostram collegerit aetas
en: Nor, if time should gather up our matter

latin: post obitum rursumque redegerit ut sita nunc est,
en: after death and bring it back again as it is now placed,

latin: atque iterum nobis fuerint data lumina vitae,
en: and the lights of life should once more be given us,

latin: pertineat quicquam tamen ad nos id quoque factum,
en: would even that event concern us in any way at all,

latin: interrupta semel cum sit repetentia nostri.
en: once the recollection of ourselves has been broken off.

latin: et nunc nil ad nos de nobis attinet, ante
en: And as it is, nothing touches us of ourselves, we who before

latin: qui fuimus, neque iam de illis nos adficit angor.
en: existed, nor does anguish over those selves affect us now.

latin: nam cum respicias inmensi temporis omne
en: For when you look back over the whole of measureless time,

latin: praeteritum spatium, tum motus materiai
en: its past expanse, and then how manifold

latin: multimodi quam sint, facile hoc adcredere possis,
en: the motions of matter are, you could easily believe this,

latin: semina saepe in eodem, ut nunc sunt, ordine posta
en: that seeds have often been set in the same order as now,

latin: haec eadem, quibus e nunc nos sumus, ante fuisse.
en: these very seeds of which we now consist, in times before.

latin: nec memori tamen id quimus reprehendere mente;
en: And yet we cannot recapture this with remembering mind;

latin: inter enim iectast vitai pausa vageque
en: for a pause of life has been thrown between, and all the motions

latin: deerrarunt passim motus ab sensibus omnes.
en: have wandered off at random, astray, far from the senses.

latin: debet enim, misere si forte aegreque futurumst;
en: For if there is to be misery and distress, perhaps,

latin: ipse quoque esse in eo tum tempore, cui male possit
en: he too must himself exist at that time, to whom ill can

latin: accidere. id quoniam mors eximit, esseque prohibet
en: befall. Since death takes this away, and prevents the existence

latin: illum cui possint incommoda conciliari,
en: of him to whom these troubles could be brought together,

latin: scire licet nobis nihil esse in morte timendum
en: we may know that there is nothing to be feared in death,

latin: nec miserum fieri qui non est posse, neque hilum
en: that he who is not cannot be wretched, and that not a whit

latin: differre an nullo fuerit iam tempore natus,
en: it differs whether he had never been born at any time,

latin: mortalem vitam mors cum inmortalis ademit.
en: when immortal death has taken away his mortal life.

latin: Proinde ubi se videas hominem indignarier ipsum,
en: Therefore, when you see a man indignant on his own behalf

latin: post mortem fore ut aut putescat corpore posto
en: that after death he will either rot, his body laid away,

latin: aut flammis interfiat malisve ferarum,
en: or perish in flames or in the jaws of wild beasts,

latin: scire licet non sincerum sonere atque subesse
en: you may know that he does not ring true, and that there lurks

latin: caecum aliquem cordi stimulum, quamvis neget ipse
en: some blind goad in his heart, however much he himself denies

latin: credere se quemquam sibi sensum in morte futurum;
en: that he believes any sense will remain to him in death.

latin: non, ut opinor, enim dat quod promittit et unde
en: For he does not, I think, grant what he professes, nor its ground,

latin: nec radicitus e vita se tollit et eicit,
en: nor tear himself up by the roots from life and cast himself out,

latin: sed facit esse sui quiddam super inscius ipse.
en: but, unknowing, makes something of himself survive.

latin: vivus enim sibi cum proponit quisque futurum,
en: For when each man, alive, pictures to himself the future,

latin: corpus uti volucres lacerent in morte feraeque,
en: that birds and beasts will tear his body in death,

latin: ipse sui miseret; neque enim se dividit illim
en: he pities himself; for he does not separate himself from it,

latin: nec removet satis a proiecto corpore et illum
en: nor withdraw enough from the body flung away, and that body

latin: se fingit sensuque suo contaminat astans.
en: he fancies is himself, and, standing by, taints with his own sense.

latin: hinc indignatur se mortalem esse creatum
en: Hence he resents that he was created mortal,

latin: nec videt in vera nullum fore morte alium se,
en: and does not see that in real death there will be no other self

latin: qui possit vivus sibi se lugere peremptum
en: who could, alive, mourn for himself destroyed,

latin: stansque iacentem se lacerari urive dolere.
en: and, standing, grieve that he lies there, torn or burned.

latin: nam si in morte malumst malis morsuque ferarum
en: For if it is an evil in death to be mauled by the jaws and bite

latin: tractari, non invenio qui non sit acerbum
en: of wild beasts, I do not find how it is not bitter

latin: ignibus inpositum calidis torrescere flammis
en: to be laid on the fire and scorched in hot flames,

latin: aut in melle situm suffocari atque rigere
en: or to be placed in honey and stifled, and to stiffen

latin: frigore, cum summo gelidi cubat aequore saxi,
en: with cold, lying on the top surface of an icy slab,

latin: urgerive superne obrutum pondere terrae.
en: or to be pressed from above, buried under the weight of earth.

latin: 'Iam iam non domus accipiet te laeta neque uxor
en: 'Now, now no glad home will receive you, nor your excellent

latin: optima, nec dulces occurrent oscula nati
en: wife, nor will your sweet children run to snatch

latin: praeripere et tacita pectus dulcedine tangent.
en: your kisses first and touch your heart with silent sweetness.

latin: non poteris factis florentibus esse tuisque
en: You will not be able to guard your flourishing affairs

latin: praesidium. misero misere' aiunt 'omnia ademit
en: and your own. Wretched man,' they say, 'wretchedly, all of them,

latin: una dies infesta tibi tot praemia vitae.'
en: one hostile day has taken from you, so many prizes of life.'

latin: illud in his rebus non addunt 'nec tibi earum
en: This they do not add in these matters: 'nor does any longing

latin: iam desiderium rerum super insidet una.'
en: for those things any longer remain with you as well.'

latin: quod bene si videant animo dictisque sequantur,
en: If they saw this rightly in mind and followed it in their words,

latin: dissoluant animi magno se angore metuque.
en: they would free themselves from great anguish and fear of mind.

latin: 'tu quidem ut es leto sopitus, sic eris aevi
en: 'You indeed, as you are now, laid asleep in death, so will you be

latin: quod super est cunctis privatus doloribus aegris;
en: for all the time that remains, freed from every grievous pain;

latin: at nos horrifico cinefactum te prope busto
en: but we, beside the horrifying pyre, you turned to ash,

latin: insatiabiliter deflevimus, aeternumque
en: have wept insatiably, and for all eternity

latin: nulla dies nobis maerorem e pectore demet.'
en: no day will take the sorrow from our hearts.'

latin: illud ab hoc igitur quaerendum est, quid sit amari
en: This, then, must be asked of him: what is so very bitter

latin: tanto opere, ad somnum si res redit atque quietem,
en: in it, if it all comes down to sleep and rest,

latin: cur quisquam aeterno possit tabescere luctu.
en: that anyone should waste away in eternal grief.

latin: Hoc etiam faciunt ubi discubuere tenentque
en: This too men often do, when they recline at table and hold

latin: pocula saepe homines et inumbrant ora coronis,
en: their cups, and shade their faces with garlands:

latin: ex animo ut dicant: 'brevis hic est fructus homullis;
en: they say from the heart: 'Brief is this fruit for poor little men;

latin: iam fuerit neque post umquam revocare licebit.'
en: soon it will have been, and never after can it be called back.'

latin: tam quam in morte mali cum primis hoc sit eorum,
en: As if in death this were chief among their evils,

latin: quod sitis exurat miseros atque arida torrat,
en: that thirst should burn the wretches and parch them dry,

latin: aut aliae cuius desiderium insideat rei.
en: or that longing for some other thing should sit upon them.

latin: nec sibi enim quisquam tum se vitamque requiret,
en: For no one misses himself and his life then,

latin: cum pariter mens et corpus sopita quiescunt;
en: when mind and body alike lie quiet in sleep;

latin: nam licet aeternum per nos sic esse soporem,
en: for as far as we care, that sleep could be everlasting,

latin: nec desiderium nostri nos adficit ullum,
en: and no longing for ourselves touches us;

latin: et tamen haud quaquam nostros tunc illa per artus
en: and yet by no means then throughout our limbs do those

latin: longe ab sensiferis primordia motibus errant,
en: first-beginnings wander far from the sense-bearing motions,

latin: cum correptus homo ex somno se colligit ipse.
en: when a man, startled from sleep, gathers himself together.

latin: multo igitur mortem minus ad nos esse putandumst,
en: Much less, then, must we think that death is to us,

latin: si minus esse potest quam quod nihil esse videmus;
en: if there can be less than what we see to be nothing;

latin: maior enim turbae disiectus materiai
en: for a greater scattering of the throng of matter

latin: consequitur leto nec quisquam expergitus extat,
en: follows on death, and no one wakes and stands up again

latin: frigida quem semel est vitai pausa secuta.
en: whom once the cold pause of life has followed.

latin: Denique si vocem rerum natura repente.
en: Finally, if the nature of things should suddenly find a voice

latin: mittat et hoc alicui nostrum sic increpet ipsa:
en: and should herself rebuke one of us in this way:

latin: 'quid tibi tanto operest, mortalis, quod nimis aegris
en: 'What ails you so, mortal, that you give yourself up too far

latin: luctibus indulges? quid mortem congemis ac fles?
en: to sick grieving? Why do you groan at death and weep?

latin: nam si grata fuit tibi vita ante acta priorque
en: For if the life you have lived till now was welcome to you,

latin: et non omnia pertusum congesta quasi in vas
en: and all its good things have not, as into a vessel full of holes,

latin: commoda perfluxere atque ingrata interiere;
en: run through and perished unenjoyed,

latin: cur non ut plenus vitae conviva recedis
en: why not withdraw like a guest who has had his fill of life,

latin: aequo animoque capis securam, stulte, quietem?
en: and with an even mind, you fool, take your untroubled rest?

latin: sin ea quae fructus cumque es periere profusa
en: But if whatever you enjoyed has been poured out and lost,

latin: vitaque in offensost, cur amplius addere quaeris,
en: and life offends you, why do you seek to add more,

latin: rursum quod pereat male et ingratum occidat omne,
en: only to be lost badly again and perish all unenjoyed,

latin: non potius vitae finem facis atque laboris?
en: and not rather make an end of life and of labor?

latin: nam tibi praeterea quod machiner inveniamque,
en: For there is nothing more that I can devise and find for you

latin: quod placeat, nihil est; eadem sunt omnia semper.
en: to please you: all things are always the same.

latin: si tibi non annis corpus iam marcet et artus
en: If your body is not yet withering with years, and your limbs

latin: confecti languent, eadem tamen omnia restant,
en: are not worn out and slack, still all things remain the same,

latin: omnia si perges vivendo vincere saecla,
en: if you should go on living to outlast all generations,

latin: atque etiam potius, si numquam sis moriturus',
en: and still more if you were never going to die.'

latin: quid respondemus, nisi iustam intendere litem
en: What do we answer, except that nature presses a just suit

latin: naturam et veram verbis exponere causam?
en: and sets out a true case in her words?

latin: grandior hic vero si iam seniorque queratur
en: But if now someone older, well on in years, should complain

latin: atque obitum lamentetur miser amplius aequo,
en: and lament his death, poor wretch, more than is right,

latin: non merito inclamet magis et voce increpet acri:
en: would she not rightly cry out louder and rebuke in a sharp voice:

latin: 'aufer abhinc lacrimas, baratre, et compesce querellas.
en: 'Away with your tears, you bottomless pit, and check your complaints.

latin: omnia perfunctus vitai praemia marces;
en: You have had all the prizes of life, and now you wither;

latin: sed quia semper aves quod abest, praesentia temnis,
en: but since you always crave what is absent and scorn what is here,

latin: inperfecta tibi elapsast ingrataque vita,
en: your life has slipped away from you unfinished and unenjoyed,

latin: et nec opinanti mors ad caput adstitit ante
en: and death, unlooked for, has taken its stand at your head

latin: quam satur ac plenus possis discedere rerum.
en: before you can depart full and sated with things.

latin: nunc aliena tua tamen aetate omnia mitte
en: As it is, let go of all things that do not suit your age,

latin: aequo animoque, age dum, magnis concede necessis?'
en: and with an even mind, come, yield to greater ones: you must.'

latin: iure, ut opinor, agat, iure increpet inciletque;
en: Rightly, I think, she would plead, rightly rebuke and reproach;

latin: cedit enim rerum novitate extrusa vetustas
en: for the old, thrust out by the newness of things, gives way

latin: semper, et ex aliis aliud reparare necessest.
en: always, and one thing must be restored out of others.

latin: Nec quisquam in barathrum nec Tartara deditur atra;
en: No one is handed down into the Pit or to black Tartarus;

latin: materies opus est, ut crescant postera saecla;
en: matter is needed, so that later generations may grow;

latin: quae tamen omnia te vita perfuncta sequentur;
en: and yet they all, their life lived through, will follow you;

latin: nec minus ergo ante haec quam tu cecidere cadentque.
en: and so, no less than you, these have fallen before and will fall.

latin: sic alid ex alio numquam desistet oriri
en: So one thing will never cease to rise from another,

latin: vitaque mancipio nulli datur, omnibus usu.
en: and life is given to none to own, to all to use.

latin: respice item quam nil ad nos ante acta vetustas
en: Look back, again, how the age gone by of eternal time

latin: temporis aeterni fuerit, quam nascimur ante.
en: before we are born was nothing to us.

latin: hoc igitur speculum nobis natura futuri
en: This, then, is the mirror nature holds up to us of the time

latin: temporis exponit post mortem denique nostram.
en: to come, after our death at last.

latin: numquid ibi horribile apparet, num triste videtur
en: Does anything horrible appear there, does anything seem

latin: quicquam, non omni somno securius exstat?
en: grim? Is it not more untroubled than any sleep?

latin: Atque ea ni mirum quae cumque Acherunte profundo
en: And indeed whatever things are told to exist

latin: prodita sunt esse, in vita sunt omnia nobis.
en: in deep Acheron, they are all here, in our life.

latin: nec miser inpendens magnum timet aereaëre saxum
en: No wretched Tantalus fears the great rock hanging in the air,

latin: Tantalus, ut famast, cassa formidine torpens;
en: as the story goes, numb with empty dread;

latin: sed magis in vita divom metus urget inanis
en: rather, in life an empty fear of the gods oppresses

latin: mortalis casumque timent quem cuique ferat fors.
en: mortals, and they fear the fall that chance may bring to each.

latin: nec Tityon volucres ineunt Acherunte iacentem
en: Nor do birds enter Tityos as he lies in Acheron,

latin: nec quod sub magno scrutentur pectore quicquam
en: nor can they truly find anything to search for

latin: perpetuam aetatem possunt reperire profecto.
en: beneath his great breast through all eternity.

latin: quam libet immani proiectu corporis exstet,
en: However vast the sprawl of his body as it lies there,

latin: qui non sola novem dispessis iugera membris
en: though with outspread limbs it should cover not just nine acres

latin: optineat, sed qui terrai totius orbem,
en: but the whole circle of the earth,

latin: non tamen aeternum poterit perferre dolorem
en: still he could not bear eternal pain

latin: nec praebere cibum proprio de corpore semper.
en: nor furnish food from his own body forever.

latin: sed Tityos nobis hic est, in amore iacentem
en: But Tityos is here among us: the one lying in love,

latin: quem volucres lacerant atque exest anxius angor
en: whom birds tear, whom anxious anguish eats away,

latin: aut alia quavis scindunt cuppedine curae.
en: or cares rend through with some other craving.

latin: Sisyphus in vita quoque nobis ante oculos est,
en: Sisyphus too is here in life before our eyes,

latin: qui petere a populo fasces saevasque secures
en: the man who seeks from the people the rods and the savage axes,

latin: imbibit et semper victus tristisque recedit.
en: thirsting for them, and always withdraws beaten and grim.

latin: nam petere imperium, quod inanest nec datur umquam,
en: For to seek power, which is empty and is never given,

latin: atque in eo semper durum sufferre laborem,
en: and always to endure hard labor for it,

latin: hoc est adverso nixantem trudere monte
en: this is to push uphill, straining against the mountain,

latin: saxum, quod tamen e summo iam vertice rusum
en: a rock which yet from the very summit rolls back again

latin: volvitur et plani raptim petit aequora campi.
en: and rushes headlong for the levels of the open plain.

latin: deinde animi ingratam naturam pascere semper
en: Then, always to feed the ungrateful nature of the mind,

latin: atque explere bonis rebus satiareque numquam,
en: to fill it with good things and never satisfy it,

latin: quod faciunt nobis annorum tempora, circum
en: as the seasons of the year do for us when they come

latin: cum redeunt fetusque ferunt variosque lepores,
en: round again and bring their offspring and their varied charms,

latin: nec tamen explemur vitai fructibus umquam,
en: and yet we are never filled with the fruits of life,

latin: hoc, ut opinor, id est, aevo florente puellas
en: this, I think, is what they mean by the girls in the flower of age

latin: quod memorant laticem pertusum congerere in vas,
en: who, they tell, pour water into a vessel full of holes,

latin: quod tamen expleri nulla ratione potestur.
en: which yet can by no means be filled.

latin: Cerberus et Furiae iam vero et lucis egestas,
en: Cerberus, too, and the Furies, and the lack of light,

latin: Tartarus horriferos eructans faucibus aestus!
en: Tartarus belching horrible blasts of heat from its jaws!

latin: qui neque sunt usquam nec possunt esse profecto;
en: These are nowhere, and indeed cannot be;

latin: sed metus in vita poenarum pro male factis
en: but in life there is fear of punishment for evil deeds,

latin: est insignibus insignis scelerisque luela,
en: notable as the deeds are notable, and atonement for crime:

latin: carcer et horribilis de saxo iactus deorsum,
en: prison, and the horrible hurling down from the rock,

latin: verbera carnifices robur pix lammina taedae;
en: scourges, executioners, the dungeon, pitch, hot plates, torches;

latin: quae tamen etsi absunt, at mens sibi conscia factis
en: and even if these are absent, the mind, conscious of its deeds,

latin: praemetuens adhibet stimulos torretque flagellis,
en: fearing beforehand, applies goads and scorches itself with whips,

latin: nec videt interea qui terminus esse malorum
en: and does not see meanwhile what limit to its evils there

latin: possit nec quae sit poenarum denique finis,
en: can be, nor what end at last to its punishments,

latin: atque eadem metuit magis haec ne in morte gravescant.
en: and fears that these same things may grow heavier in death.

latin: hic Acherusia fit stultorum denique vita.
en: Here, in the end, the life of fools becomes an Acheron.

latin: Hoc etiam tibi tute interdum dicere possis.
en: This too you might at times say to yourself:

latin: 'lumina sis oculis etiam bonus Ancus reliquit,
en: 'Even good Ancus has left the light with his eyes,

latin: qui melior multis quam tu fuit, improbe, rebus.
en: who was better than you, you shameless one, in many things.

latin: inde alii multi reges rerumque potentes
en: Since then many other kings and lords of things

latin: occiderunt, magnis qui gentibus imperitarunt.
en: have perished, who ruled over great nations.

latin: ille quoque ipse, viam qui quondam per mare magnum
en: He too, the very one who once laid a road across the great sea

latin: stravit iterque dedit legionibus ire per altum
en: and gave his legions a way to go over the deep

latin: ac pedibus salsas docuit super ire lucunas
en: and taught them to cross the salt lagoons on foot

latin: et contempsit equis insultans murmura ponti,
en: and, trampling with his horses, scorned the roar of the sea,

latin: lumine adempto animam moribundo corpore fudit.
en: robbed of the light, poured out his spirit from a dying body.

latin: Scipiadas, belli fulmen, Carthaginis horror,
en: The son of the Scipios, thunderbolt of war, terror of Carthage,

latin: ossa dedit terrae proinde ac famul infimus esset.
en: gave his bones to the earth as if he were the lowest servant.

latin: adde repertores doctrinarum atque leporum,
en: Add the discoverers of learning and of graces,

latin: adde Heliconiadum comites; quorum unus Homerus
en: add the companions of the Heliconian Muses; among them Homer,

latin: sceptra potitus eadem aliis sopitus quietest.
en: who alone held the scepter, sleeps in the same rest as the others.

latin: denique Democritum post quam matura vetustas
en: Finally Democritus, after ripe old age

latin: admonuit memores motus languescere mentis,
en: warned him that the remembering motions of his mind were slackening,

latin: sponte sua leto caput obvius optulit ipse.
en: went of his own will to meet death and offered up his head.

latin: ipse Epicurus obit decurso lumine vitae,
en: Epicurus himself died, the light of his life run through,

latin: qui genus humanum ingenio superavit et omnis
en: he who surpassed the human race in genius and put out

latin: restinxit stellas exortus ut aetherius sol.
en: all the stars, as the sun in the ether does, once risen.

latin: tu vero dubitabis et indignabere obire?
en: And will you hesitate, and resent it, to die?

latin: mortua cui vita est prope iam vivo atque videnti,
en: You, whose life is all but dead while you still live and see,

latin: qui somno partem maiorem conteris aevi,
en: who waste the greater part of your life in sleep,

latin: et viligans stertis nec somnia cernere cessas
en: and snore while awake, and never cease to see dreams,

latin: sollicitamque geris cassa formidine mentem
en: and carry a mind troubled with empty dread,

latin: nec reperire potes tibi quid sit saepe mali, cum
en: and often cannot find what is wrong with you, when,

latin: ebrius urgeris multis miser undique curis
en: drunk, poor wretch, you are pressed by many cares on every side

latin: atque animo incerto fluitans errore vagaris.'
en: and drift wandering in the wavering error of your mind.'

latin: Si possent homines, proinde ac sentire videntur
en: If men could, just as they plainly feel

latin: pondus inesse animo, quod se gravitate fatiget,
en: a weight lies in the mind, wearing them out with its heaviness,

latin: e quibus id fiat causis quoque noscere et unde
en: also come to know from what causes it arises, and from where

latin: tanta mali tam quam moles in pectore constet,
en: so great a mass, as it were, of evil stands in the breast,

latin: haut ita vitam agerent, ut nunc plerumque videmus
en: they would not live their lives as now we mostly see them,

latin: quid sibi quisque velit nescire et quaerere semper,
en: each not knowing what he wants for himself, and always seeking

latin: commutare locum, quasi onus deponere possit.
en: to change his place, as if he could set his burden down.

latin: exit saepe foras magnis ex aedibus ille,
en: Often he goes out of doors from his great house,

latin: esse domi quem pertaesumst, subitoque revertit,
en: who is weary to death of home, and suddenly comes back,

latin: quippe foris nihilo melius qui sentiat esse.
en: since indeed he feels himself no better off outside.

latin: currit agens mannos ad villam praecipitanter
en: He races to his villa, driving his ponies headlong,

latin: auxilium tectis quasi ferre ardentibus instans;
en: as if pressing on to bring help to a house on fire;

latin: oscitat extemplo, tetigit cum limina villae,
en: he yawns at once, the moment he has touched the villa's threshold,

latin: aut abit in somnum gravis atque oblivia quaerit,
en: or goes off heavily into sleep and looks for forgetfulness,

latin: aut etiam properans urbem petit atque revisit.
en: or even hurries back to make for the city and see it again.

latin: hoc se quisque modo fugit, at quem scilicet, ut fit,
en: So each man flees himself, yet that self, as happens, of course,

latin: effugere haut potis est: ingratius haeret et odit
en: he cannot escape; he clings to it against his will, and hates it,

latin: propterea, morbi quia causam non tenet aeger;
en: because, sick as he is, he does not grasp the cause of his disease;

latin: quam bene si videat, iam rebus quisque relictis
en: if he saw it clearly, each man would leave his affairs behind

latin: naturam primum studeat cognoscere rerum,
en: and study first of all to know the nature of things,

latin: temporis aeterni quoniam, non unius horae,
en: since it is the state of eternal time, not of a single hour,

latin: ambigitur status, in quo sit mortalibus omnis
en: that is in question, the state in which mortals must spend all

latin: aetas, post mortem quae restat cumque manendo.
en: the age that remains to be waited out after death.

latin: Denique tanto opere in dubiis trepidare periclis
en: Finally, to tremble so much amid doubtful dangers,

latin: quae mala nos subigit vitai tanta cupido?
en: what great and evil craving for life compels us?

latin: certe equidem finis vitae mortalibus adstat
en: Surely an end of life stands waiting for mortals,

latin: nec devitari letum pote, quin obeamus.
en: and death cannot be avoided: we must go to meet it.

latin: praeterea versamur ibidem atque insumus usque
en: Further, we turn about in the same place and stay there always,

latin: nec nova vivendo procuditur ulla voluptas;
en: and no new pleasure is hammered out by living;

latin: sed dum abest quod avemus, id exsuperare videtur
en: but while what we long for is absent, it seems to surpass

latin: cetera; post aliud, cum contigit illud, avemus
en: the rest; then, when that has come, we long for something else,

latin: et sitis aequa tenet vitai semper hiantis.
en: and an equal thirst for life holds us, always gaping.

latin: posteraque in dubiost fortunam quam vehat aetas,
en: And it is in doubt what fortune the coming age will carry,

latin: quidve ferat nobis casus quive exitus instet.
en: or what chance will bring us, or what end is at hand.

latin: nec prorsum vitam ducendo demimus hilum
en: Nor by prolonging life do we take away one jot

latin: tempore de mortis nec delibare valemus,
en: from the time of death, nor can we subtract anything from it

latin: quo minus esse diu possimus forte perempti.
en: so that, once destroyed, we might perhaps be dead for less long.

latin: proinde licet quod vis vivendo condere saecla,
en: Therefore you may live out as many generations as you like;

latin: mors aeterna tamen nihilo minus illa manebit,
en: that eternal death will be waiting for you none the less,

latin: nec minus ille diu iam non erit, ex hodierno
en: and he will be no more for no less long who, with today's

latin: lumine qui finem vitai fecit, et ille,
en: light, made an end of life, than he

latin: mensibus atque annis qui multis occidit ante.
en: who perished many months and years before.
